summary: Google Products flicker (QA-002) had no frame-by-frame pixel evidence: consecutive PNGs hashed differently on the target and on a static control, and a byte hash cannot say whether content moved.
evidence: Closed by BR-286 (scripts/live-frame-stability.py), measured 2026-11-14 on https://about.google/products/ at 1280x1024 dpr 1, 5 captures 1000ms apart, two independent navigations of the same binary (sha b90d2acb...), with the same readings reproduced on 2026-11-13 (sha 7931602d...): verdict STABLE, exit 0. Goosie changes 0 px in every content region of every consecutive pair, its ink count is 735,576 on all 20 captures, and every capture is self-reported complete (idle, 0 tiles needed, 0 bytes painting). The two 2026-11-14 navigations differ by exactly 0 px on all 25 cross pairs, so the QA-002 observation that consecutive PNGs hashed differently was never a content change - which is the reading docs/qa-test-plan.md QA-002 forbids closing on in the first place. Scope, stated because the close must not read as more than it is: this is the unscrolled viewport, which is QA-002's first half. The plan's second half (scroll one screen down and repeat the five captures) still cannot be measured - no capture path scrolls before it shoots - and that residual is registered as GOOSIE-SEQSCROLL-001 rather than being closed under this id. What the same measurement does show is two other things, registered separately instead of being swept under this id: the page is not static in the reference (Chromium 131.0.6778.33 changes band y=194..233 by 16,818-18,021 px per pair, Goosie by 0) -> GOOSIE-PAGEANIM-001, and Goosie paints nothing where Chromium's top band sits (y=16..47) -> GOOSIE-TOPBAND-001.

owner: scripts/live-frame-stability.py (scrolled pass) - the capture path is done, see BR-287
summary: A live capture sequence can only shoot the top of a page, so QA-002's second half - scroll one screen down and repeat the five captures - has no evidence path and the smoke case cannot be fully closed.
evidence: docs/qa-test-plan.md QA-002 asks for five idle captures, then the same five after scrolling one screen down. cmd/goosie/config.go:102 shows the only scripted-scroll driver is -gate (`drive -frames scripted scroll frames at real pacing, then report`), and the -screenshot/-screenshot-seq path (config.go:102-107, drive.go steadyDriver) has no scroll input at all: grep for `scroll` in cmd/goosie/config.go returns the -gate help line and nothing else. scripts/live-frame-stability.py therefore measures whatever y-offset the page lands on after load, which for https://about.google/products/ is the top (measured 2026-11-14, 1280x1024). The consequence is that GOOSIE-RENDER-001 could only be closed for the unscrolled viewport, and QA-002 stays PARTIAL until a sequence run can be pointed at a scrolled position. This is a missing capability of the measurement path, not a claim that scrolled pages flicker: nothing has been measured either way below the fold. ADDENDUM 2026-11-14, capability landed, measurement still open. `-seq-scroll-screens N` exists (QC case BR-287, 5 oracles in cmd/goosie/sequence_test.go): one press = the engine's own screen law (`scrollScreenHeight`, 9/10 of the viewport height, now shared with `scrollContentKey` so PageDown and the sequence cannot drift apart), applied to the frame path's viewport plus `SyncViewportScroll` so window.scrollY agrees with the pixels, held until two further frames have been drawn, and recorded as `scroll_screens`/`scroll_presses`/`scroll_landed` plus a per-frame `scroll_y` read back from the clamped viewport. Measured on the new fixture at 600x400 DPR 1: unscrolled run inks 0 px of a marker placed at content y 640..700 and reports scroll_y 0; `-seq-scroll-screens 1` reports scroll_screens 1, scroll_presses 1, scroll_landed true, scroll_y 360 on every capture, the marker inked in both captures, and 0 px changed between them; `-seq-scroll-screens 3` on a 400px page still writes all 3 captures with scroll_landed false and scroll_y 0. What remains for this entry is the measurement, not the capability: scripts/live-frame-stability.py still shoots only the top of the page, so docs/qa-test-plan.md QA-002's second half ('scroll one screen down and repeat') has no numbers yet, and GOOSIE-SCROLLCEILING-001 will clamp a live page whose lower blocks paint nothing. Red before the feature, measured with the four cmd/goosie implementation files stashed and the test file unchanged: 'vet: cmd/goosie/sequence_test.go:413:40: undefined: seqScroll' fails the package build, and at binary level the run dies with 'run: usage: flag provided but not defined: -seq-scroll-screens' (0.47s and 0.00s). ADDENDUM 2026-11-14, CLOSED by BR-288 (60f0d528): scripts/live-frame-stability.py now runs one pass per scroll position - `top` (0 screens) then `scrolled` (--scroll-screens N, default 1) - one navigation per engine per pass, so QA-002's second half has numbers. Measured 2026-11-14 19:20 +0700 on https://about.google/products/, binary sha 5938f539188bfefc..., Chromium 131.0.6778.33, 1280x1024 dpr 1, 5 captures x 1000ms per pass: `VERDICT STABLE across passes: top=STABLE, scrolled=STABLE`, exit 0. The scrolled pass sat at y=921 = scrollScreenHeight(1024) = 1024*9/10 with scroll_presses 1 and scroll_landed true, found 7 content regions, and reported 0 unstable regions and ink spread 0 for Goosie; Chromium reported 0 unstable regions at the same offset, so the question QA-002 actually asks - does a static area flicker - is answered `no` at both positions. A pass is refused rather than scored when the two engines cannot agree about where they were: the tool reads Goosie's own per-capture scroll_y out of frames.json, drives Chromium with window.scrollTo to exactly that number, reads window.scrollY back, and marks the parity axis refused if the two differ or if Goosie's five captures hold more than one offset. Both refusals were exercised on the live page: `--scroll-screens 20` printed `parity refused: goosie sat at y=18420 while Chromium sat at y=6832` (Chromium's maximum for that document). And a pass whose captures carry no ink is refused too - the same 20-screen run had printed STABLE over five blank frames before that gate existed, which is the failure mode this entry would otherwise have re-opened. What the scrolled pass measured below the fold is a different defect and is registered as GOOSIE-SCROLLRANGE-001; docs/qa-test-plan.md QA-002 and catalog rows BR-287/BR-288 carry the numbers.

Implementing ::first-letter removed none of them. (2) Those three bands are not missing content at all: Goosie paints the lines, ~20px away from Chromium's band rows, so the blank test fires on vertical drift. For band (457,475) Goosie has ink rows 437-455 and 483-498 and none in between, and the crop shows 'This paragraph has a checkmark after it' rendered with its checkmark. See GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001. Priority lowered P1 -> P2 on this measurement; the ::before/::after content in the same fixture renders, and the residual band count is an artifact of the metric, not of this defect.

summary: TestNativeEndToEndPlaysARealVideo is load-sensitive: under a busy machine it can time out, which risks a false red in the sweep's gate step.
evidence:
test/engine/media_native_test.go:218. Observed while running full suites in parallel worktrees; TASK-029 §3 forbids raising the timeout as a fix, so it is recorded here instead. Same class observed on 2026-10-25 at 20:07: TestFootprintAtRestIsBoundedByConfiguredCaches reported retained=257.03 MiB against configured=207.10 MiB while 14 orphaned busy-loop shells from an old stress command held the 1-minute load average near 90; the identical run passed at 2.29s on the same commit (130bc9a) once the load was removed. The at-rest footprint criterion is therefore load-sensitive and must be measured on an idle machine, never in parallel with another suite.
THIRD INSTANCE, 2026-10-26 (integrator): `TestWarmScrollRasterizesNoTiles` in `test/surface` failed once while `go test -count=1 ./...` ran on the TASK-047 branch alongside concurrent agent builds, with `Reused = 92 after 24 tile-aligned frames, want 96: four cached tiles per frame went uncounted`. Re-run evidence: the test passed 3/3 on main, 5/5 in the branch isolated, 3/3 for the whole `test/surface` package, and a full-suite rerun returned rc 0 on both main and the branch. Same class as the two above - a counter budget tied to a warm-up that load can stretch - not a regression from TASK-047; recorded here so a future red is recognised before anyone bisects.

summary: Button-level formnovalidate was not honoured on every activation path, and a disabled form control still received clicks, still toggled, and still let implicit submission fall through to the next enabled submit button.
evidence:
grep -rn formnovalidate internal/engine returns no matches, while the merged bypass oracle test/engine/form_submission_test.go:TestFormNovalidateBypass only exercises the form-level novalidate attribute. WHATWG HTML 4.10.13.3.6 step 9 collects and honours the submitter's novalidate state; ValidateForm (internal/engine/forms.go) reads only the form attribute.

Closed by BR-279 (docs/qa-test-catalog.md) on 2026-11-13. The submitter's novalidate state was already read at the engine (forms.go: submitterSkipsValidation, landed in b42b5fd4); what this slice did is measure the whole activation surface around it and pin it, and the measurement exposed the disabled-control half, which turned out to be the broken part.

Measured law, all of it from a hit log rather than from prose (Playwright + a socketserver recording navigations, /tmp/v2/probe1..probe11.html, Chromium 131.0.6778.33, one page reload per case so a form.submit() navigation cannot destroy accumulated state): clicking the plain submit button of a form whose required control is empty records no request, clicking its formnovalidate sibling records /s1?q1=; formnovalidate="", FORMNOVALIDATE and formnovalidate="false" all submit, so presence decides and the value decides nothing; <button type=button formnovalidate> records nothing because it is not a submit button; input[type=submit formnovalidate] submits; implicit Enter uses the first submit button in tree order as its submitter (/s2?q2= when that button carries formnovalidate, [] when it is plain, /s3?q3= when the form has only the skip button).

The disabled half, which is what actually needed fixing: a press on a disabled button/checkbox/text/reset shows only pointerdown@X,pointerup@X at the document's capture listeners - no mousedown, no mouseup, no click - the checkbox stays unchecked and activeElement does not change; a press on a <span> wrapped inside a disabled submit button records click:ins alone, with the button's, the form's and the document's own listeners silent, i.e. the click path is cut at the control's boundary, while the same span's element.click() from JS bubbles fully as click:ins,click:bsub,click:f1 and still submits nothing, and bsub.click() dispatches nothing at all; <fieldset disabled> and a stray <div disabled> keep their clicks (click:fs2, click:ddiv) because neither is a control; f2.requestSubmit(dbtn2 disabled) fires a submit event whose submitter is dbtn2 and whose query is /s2?t2=keep - a disabled submitter contributes no name/value pair, the enabled one in the same slot gives /s2?t2=keep&e2=1; f2.requestSubmit() reports submitter null; Enter while the first submit button is disabled records no navigation and no invalid event, and deleting the disabled attribute lets the same Enter submit /s2?t2=t2v; checkValidity and reportValidity on the empty-required form answer [false,false]; the IDL reads the attribute, writing formNoValidate = true gives [true,"",true] and false gives [false,false], and form[novalidate].noValidate is true.

Goosie at b10fffbe was wrong on four counts: a click on a disabled submit queued /s1?q1= with the button's and the form's listeners firing, a disabled checkbox toggled to checked, disabled text and reset controls received clicks, a press on the span inside a disabled button delivered the click to the button (click:boff fired, click:ins did not), Enter with a disabled first button silently used the enabled second one (/s2?t2=keep&e2=1), and <div disabled>.click() dispatched nothing because the guard tested IsFormControlDisabled instead of asking whether the node is a control at all. The requestSubmit, IDL and validity shapes were already right and are pinned anyway, as drift guards.

Oracle: test/engine/form_submitter_novalidate_test.go, 12 tests tagged // qc:BR-279. Red on HEAD (clean worktree at b10fffbe, only the test files copied in): 10 assertions across 6 tests / 7 subtests. Attribution by mutation on the fixed tree: M1 delete the ClickAt block - 7 assertions / 3 tests / 6 subtests; M2 delete the ToggleControl guard - 1 / 1; M3a delete the Enter block - 1 / 1; M3b let FirstSubmitButton filter disabled again - 1 / 1 on the same test, which is what separates the choosing of a submitter from the blocking of one; M4 restore the wide js guard - 1 / 1 on exactly the strayDivClick line. Reverting everything returns the suite to green.

No render fixture: nothing here is visible in a frame, and the precedent for event-behaviour cases is BR-105/BR-107, both INT-only. Three residuals this slice measured and deliberately did not fix are registered as GOOSIE-MOUSESEQ-001, GOOSIE-LABELACTIVATE-001 and GOOSIE-VALIDFOCUS-001.

summary: Browser-level tests read the layout arena from the test goroutine, so the journeys that decide whether a feature works are unsynchronised against the engine's input goroutine.
evidence: 14 sites in cmd/goosie/*_test.go walk sess.Arena.Objects directly (cmd/goosie/e2e_test.go:185 clickElementByID, clipboard_test.go:36,118, form_nav_test.go:57,125,237, ...). TASK-030's -race run proved the same class of cross-goroutine DOM read is unsafe, and the locking contract requires locked Session accessors. A mutation that rebuilds layout can therefore produce a torn read or an unsynchronised click coordinate instead of a clean failure.

summary: The tab scroll-restore journey asserts a cross-tab inequality instead of an exact offset, so it can pass for the wrong reason or fail when both tabs clamp to the same scroll extent.
evidence: cmd/goosie/journey_p1_tabs_test.go:89-98 presses PageDown twice in tab 2 and waits for active.ScrollY() > tab1Scroll, comparing one tab's offset against a different tab's; the same test then asserts exact equality (== tab1Scroll, == tab2Scroll) at lines 121 and 132. The inequality oracle depends on page heights and clamp values, and it is the assertion that failed twice under machine load. Re-measured 2026-10-26 on 6071b8b: 3 failures in 45 iterations of -race runs (-count=5: 1, -count=8: 1, -count=8: 0, -count=24: 1) and in the -count=24 run the failure was the FIRST iteration of a freshly built test binary while the 23 later iterations each took 0.16s and passed - the failing one spent its 8.12s inside this wait, so cold-start load is the trigger, not random scheduling. Two candidate mechanisms were measured and dismissed: (i) surface.mergeEvent folding two PageDown presses into one - a burst of four bare pressKey injections with no wait produced exactly four pages (one page 432, burst total 2160), so at steady state discrete keys are not lost; (ii) scrollContentTo computing the target from the shared scheduler viewport while ScrollY is per-tab - in 20/20 -race runs tab 2's ScrollY equalled sched.Viewport().Offset.Y at both steps (432/432 then 864/864). Replacing the second press with a wheel delta made the test fail 30/30, which is registered on its own as GOOSIE-WHEEL-001, so the oracle stays as written and the mechanism that parks tab 2 at tab 1's offset on a cold binary stays unidentified.

summary: On https://about.google/products/ Goosie paints nothing above row 185 while Chromium's first inked row is 16, so the page's top band is missing and worst_iou is pinned at 0.0 on every capture.
evidence: Measured 2026-11-14 by scripts/live-frame-stability.py (BR-286) on the same 20 captures that cleared GOOSIE-RENDER-001, viewport 1280x1024 dpr 1, Chromium 131.0.6778.33, parity helpers from testdata/parity.py (INK_CUTOFF 245, MIN_INK 200, BAND_GAP 6). Region y=16..47 x=17..501: Chromium 2,703 ink px (density 0.1745, 395 distinct colours) against Goosie 0 ink px (density 0.0000, 1 colour). Rows 0..120 average 23.675 ink px per row in Chromium and 0 in Goosie. The content is displaced rather than wholly absent: rows 120..193 carry 548 ink px in Goosie and 0 in Chromium, and Goosie's first inked row anywhere is 185 against Chromium's 16. This is the only truly-blank band in the run and it is what holds worst_iou at 0.0 for all 10 captures while pct_exact sits at 84.70-84.81 and coverage at 1.127-1.130. Not root-caused: the visible candidates are the header/logo subtree (an image or a CSS feature that suppresses its box) and whatever pushes the rest of the page down; neither is claimed here. Priority is a judgement - the page is readable and 735,576 ink px are painted, so this is not the LIVE-001 blank-window family - and a human may re-rank it.

summary: A live page that animates itself does not animate in Goosie: band y=194..233 changes 16,818-18,021 px per capture pair in Chromium and 0 px in Goosie across 20 captures, so the frame path never sees work the page's own script produces.
evidence: Measured 2026-11-14 (reproduced 2026-11-13) by scripts/live-frame-stability.py (BR-286) on https://about.google/products/ at 1280x1024 dpr 1, 5 captures 1000ms apart per run, tolerance parity.THRESHOLD = 30 per channel, regions from parity.content_bands of the Chromium reference (6 regions). Goosie: 0 px changed in every region of every consecutive pair, ink constant at 735,576, every capture complete (idle, 0 tiles needed, 0 bytes painting), presents still climbing 36 -> 399, so the loop is running and is not the reason nothing moves. Chromium 131.0.6778.33: region y=194..233 x=0..1266 changes on all four pairs (18,021 / 17,940 / 17,371 / 17,108 in run A; 17,689 / 18,009 / 17,536 / 16,818 in run B) and no other region moves, with ink spread 692 and 1,098. Leading candidate, from the run's own stderr and the only uncaught error of the session: https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/reviewed-scripts/gtm/gtm.js?id=GTM-WQZB4J&cookieCategory=2A:1: TypeError: Cannot read property 'src' of undefined - if that script drives the banner, the animation dies with it. Timer- and RAF-driven repaint itself is covered offline by BR-255 and BR-082, so this is not a missing capability claim about the scheduler; it is a measured absence of any pixel change on a page the reference animates. Root cause unconfirmed - do not close this entry without re-running the tool and naming the script.

owner: internal/css + internal/style + internal/layout as they apply to the top viewport of about.google/products (unresolved)
summary: Fixing the minified at-rule prelude (GOOSIE-ATPRELUDE-001) made the top-of-page capture of about.google/products match Chromium on FEWER pixels within the parity tolerance - 84.71-84.79% -> 77.94-77.99% - while ink and coverage both moved toward Chromium. Measured, not explained: the cause is not determined here.
evidence: GOOSIE-TOPPARITY-001. Found by the A/B of the prelude fix, recorded because a fix that improves one axis and regresses another must not be shipped on the strength of the improvement alone. Measurement, scripts/live-frame-stability.py top pass (y=0), 1280x1024 dpr 1, 5 captures x 1000ms, Chromium 131.0.6778.33, Goosie binary sha 7116e630... (pre) vs ce1f22c1... (post, two runs) - artifacts /tmp/b289x-live-pre.json, -post.json and -after.json; the post number was reproduced on two independent runs and again on the final binary in a two-capture run with the PNGs kept (/tmp/b289x-top-pre.json, /tmp/b289x-top-post.json). WITHIN-TOLERANCE (parity.THRESHOLD 30 per channel, whole frame): 84.72/84.70/84.79/84.79/84.75 -> 77.94/77.94/77.98/77.98/77.96. STRICT-EXACT (zero tolerance, whole frame): 41.535 -> 53.811 - the two metrics disagree, and the disagreement is where the information is. Coverage 1.127-1.129 -> 1.049-1.051 and Goosie ink 735,576 -> 566,970 against Chromium's 458,119-458,295, i.e. Goosie paints 168,606 fewer inked px and its ink total moves from 1.60x the oracle to 1.24x. A pixel-set split of the same two frames says which pixels: white-in-both rises 544,116 -> 703,981 while 'white in Goosie but inked in Chromium' falls 263,675 -> 103,867, so the strict-exact gain is Goosie stopping painting where Chromium paints nothing and starting where Chromium paints ink. Row-band deltas (64px bands, within-tolerance) localise the loss below y=640: 640..703 -39.3, 704..767 -49.3, 896..959 -47.3, 960..1023 -27.5, 832..895 -19.5, 320..383 -8.1, while 448..575 gains 78.5 and 94.2 points of strict-exact and 576..639 gains 41.4 within-tolerance; in the y>=640 bands strict-exact stays ~0 on BOTH binaries, so that region never matched glyph-for-glyph and the within-tolerance fall is a reposition, not a colour change. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: no cause. The candidates this slice can name but not separate are (a) content that legitimately moved down into Chromium's place and now overlaps a different subtree, (b) the top band displacement already registered as GOOSIE-TOPBAND-001, which the same fix shifted but did not remove (blank_bands stays [16,47] on both binaries, worst_iou stays 0.0), and (c) per-navigation variation of the live page - though the two post-fix runs and the two pre-fix runs agree with each other to 0.05 points, so variation is not what produced the fall. Caveat for whoever picks this up: the band table compares two navigations of a live page, so its attribution is suggestive; the whole-frame numbers, each scored against that run's own Chromium capture, are the like-for-like evidence. summary: A select's submitted value is raw option text content and the first selected option wins, so Goosie sends whitespace the server never sees from Chromium and resolves multi-selected markup to the wrong option.
evidence:

  Charcoal
" for an option whose text content is '
  Charcoal
' and encoded it as c=%0A++Charcoal%0A, while Chromium/Playwright normalises the same shape to option.textContent = '  Hi
  there
' -> option.value === 'Hi there' (strip plus internal whitespace collapse). For a <select> with two selected options Chromium reports selectedIndex 1, value 'b', formdata 'b' (last wins) whereas SelectedOption (internal/engine/focus.go:556) returns the first.   Charcoal
", want "Charcoal"; SelectedOption resolving first-wins -> rc 1, submitted c = "a", want "b" and value before any key = "1", want 2; routing the value attribute through the normaliser -> rc 1, encoded form = "c=pad+me", want "c=++pad++me++". evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-001. Measured by testdata/live-parity.py against Chromium/Playwright at viewport 1280x1024, dpr 1, wait_until=load, screenshots viewport-only on both sides.
