owner: internal/platform/darwin (AX marshal) + ARIA heading-level edge parity
summary: Narrowed 2026-11-14 by BR-300 (bcf0f264): the heading role and its level now live in the engine accessibility tree (ax.Node.Level, set by headingLevel from the tag 1..6 or a valid aria-level). Two residuals keep this open. (1) The native macOS bridge does not marshal Level, so VoiceOver still cannot hear heading depth. (2) An invalid or out-of-range aria-level diverges from Chromium on a measured quirk that was deliberately not mimicked.
evidence: GOOSIE-AX-002. The original summary - 'the accessibility tree has no heading role: the role vocabulary stops at 13 roles' - was falsified by the current tree: internal/ax/ax.go now carries RoleHeading (and RoleListBox), and BR-300 gave it Level. What closing needs, restated: (1) internal/platform/darwin must marshal ax.Node.Level (and the Props channel) across the AX bridge - today the marshal sends role/identifier/label/value/href/flags and drops both Level and Props, so a macOS assistive client gets no heading depth even though the engine tree has it; this needs a display-bearing host to verify with a real assistive client. (2) aria-level that fails to parse or falls outside 1..6: Chromium collapses a native h4 to level 1 (a native->1 collapse that is itself inconsistent, since a bare ARIA heading defaults to 2), while Goosie ignores the invalid value and keeps the implicit tag level (h4 -> 4). BR-300 measured this and chose NOT to mimic the quirk, pinning the engine behaviour instead; matching Chromium on that branch is an open question. Neither residual blocks the clean cases - h1..h6 -> 1..6, valid aria-level override, and ARIA default 2 are all measured to match Chromium via Accessibility.getFullAXTree and pinned by three // qc:BR-300 oracles in test/engine/accessibility_heading_level_test.go. Status stays open until the darwin marshal is verified and the invalid-aria-level decision is resolved.

summary: A live sweep names its report after the commit that was HEAD when it finished, not the build whose pixels it measured, so a sweep that runs across a merge attributes reference-browser noise to engine commits that never ran.
evidence: Discovered while attributing sweep docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T2045Z-ec0f7fb9. run_id is built at report-write time: testdata/live-parity.py:694 calls _sha8(), which at :711-716 shells out to `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD` - the pixels were captured 13 minutes earlier. Proof of the gap on this host: `make live-parity` depends on `build` (Makefile:68), and bin/goosie carries mtime 2026-10-25T20:31:52Z, the sweep start, while main moved through 0cefc1d (20:34:36Z), bcfab51 (20:37:59Z) and ec0f7fb (20:44:00Z) before the report was written at 20:45Z. So that report's rows describe the engine as of 6071b8b - the same sources the previous sweep 2026-10-25T2017Z-6071b8b9 measured, because the only commit in between (193de74, 20:33:16Z) touches docs/qa-live-parity and docs/qa-open-defects.json alone. Consequence read the right way: all four label flips between the two sweeps (sggp.org.vn LOW_COVERAGE -> FETCH_FAILED, aljazeera.com OK -> FETCH_FAILED, thanhnien.vn MISSING_REGIONS -> LOW_COVERAGE, nike.com MISSING_REGIONS -> OK) and the noise-floor jump (its own repeated 12-site pass: max |delta_pct_exact| 3.45 in sweep 4, 18.36 in sweep 5, on vnexpress.net, no label flipped in either) happened with identical engine code, so none of them is an engine result - which is exactly what GOOSIE-LIVE-004 and GOOSIE-LIVE-007 predict. What closing needs: name the report by the built binary (record `git rev-parse HEAD` at build time, or hash the binary itself into the JSON), and say so in the header line the reader sees first. CLOSED by TASK-045, re-measured by the integrator on this host before the merge (ca39672): capture_build() now runs at the start of the sweep, before the first page is fetched, and records the source SHA (full and short) plus the binary path and its SHA-256; the report file name and the JSON run_id are derived from that snapshot (`report_sha8`), never from write-time HEAD. Proofs run here, not read from the branch report: `python3 testdata/live-parity.py --selftest` exits 0 with 49 PASS, including a check that an unreadable binary is recorded as unhashed rather than guessed; deleting the JSON `build` key (testdata/live-parity.py:503) exits 1 with two checks red ('the JSON names the source SHA, the binary path and the binary SHA-256 - null', and the markdown first-lines check reporting UNKNOWN); a real 8-URL sweep against a freshly built binary wrote 2026-10-25T2145Z-0514d6d7.md whose first line names source `0514d6d7` and binary SHA-256 `79784739169147783f130d2fe320e87fac99d34a19af47ef66dc48f681b4719f`, and the JSON gained exactly one top-level key (`build`) with nothing removed. Regression the branch caused and disclosed itself: folding the SHA-8 helper into `_git_rev(abbrev)` dropped the `HEAD` argument, so a real sweep printed `source UNKNOWN` and named the file `-unknown.md`; that is now gated by three selftest checks. Reads on the record: sweeps #1-#5 keep their write-time names and must be interpreted through this entry's evidence rather than re-baselined, and sweep #6 onward is the first series whose attribution to a build is trustworthy. REOPENED by the integrator on 2026-10-26, and my own closure claim is withdrawn in this entry rather than quietly edited away. Sweep `docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T2212Z-4302e3cb` is the counter-example: its `run_id` and filename end in `4302e3cb` — HEAD when the report was WRITTEN — while `build.source_sha8` in the same JSON says `9754fda4`, the build that produced the pixels. The sentence I wrote when closing said 'the report file name and the JSON run_id are derived from that snapshot (`report_sha8`), never from write-time HEAD'; the code says otherwise at `testdata/live-parity.py:1093` (`run_id = strftime(...) + '-' + _sha8()`), so only the header, the JSON `build` block and the WARNING line were ever derived from the capture. Why my own verification missed it: the 8-URL probe run I used as proof finished without main moving, so write-time and capture-time SHAs were equal and the check at :991 (`report_names_measured_build is True`) could not distinguish the two behaviours — the branch's selftest at :970 asserts only that the mismatch is *detected*, not that the filename avoids it. What is genuinely fixed and stays fixed: the run captures `git rev-parse HEAD` plus the binary path and SHA-256 before the first fetch, the markdown says so in the first lines, the JSON carries a `build` block with nothing removed, and a sweep whose name blames the wrong commit now prints that fact in its own header (`WARNING - the filename names a different commit than these pixels`). What is still open: name the artifact from `build.report_sha8` captured at start, so the file name agrees with the pixels it reports; until then every sweep record must be attributed from the JSON `build.source_sha8`, not from its filename - which is how this sweep's record is written. FIRED FOR REAL on sweep 8 (2026-10-26): the integrator committed a defect registration while the ~20-minute run was in flight, so HEAD moved from `a5c54245` to `2a254fb2` between build capture and report write. The artifact is therefore named `2026-10-26T0204Z-2a254fb2` while `build.source_sha8` says `a5c54245`, and `build.report_names_measured_build` is `false` — the header warning printed exactly as designed, and the sweep record was attributed from the JSON field. Operationally: do not commit during a live sweep, or read `build.source_sha8` before quoting any filename. The open half is unchanged — name the artifact from the `report_sha8` captured at start so the filename and the pixels always agree.

summary: Group opacity is multiplied per command at tile-raster time instead of compositing the faded group once offscreen, so two translucent layers sharing one `opacity` group darken twice.
evidence: GOOSIE-COMPOSITE-001 - disclosed by TASK-044 §5.9 and measured independently by the integrator on 2026-10-26 (`/tmp/t46-check/group.html`, 300x120 DPR 1: a container with `opacity:0.5` holding two `rgba(0,0,255,0.5)` 60x60 boxes overlapping by 30 px). Single-box pixel agrees with Chromium exactly: goosie (191,191,255) vs chromium (191,191,255). The overlap does not: goosie (143,143,255) vs chromium (158,158,255), i.e. 0.25 applied twice (effective 0.4375) where the spec asks for 0.75 composited inside the group and the group once at 0.5 (effective 0.375). Root: `internal/raster/tile.go` reads `DisplayCmd.Opacity` per command, so nothing in the engine ever holds a group buffer; TASK-044 fixed which commands exist and what alpha each carries, not how they are combined. Blast radius: only visible when two translucent paintings overlap inside one faded group - non-overlapping boxes and non-faded groups agree with Chromium, which is why the parity corpus (87/87, average 96.14%) does not catch it and no fixture of mine is scored on it. What closing needs: an offscreen group buffer (or equivalent per-group composite) at the tile raster, a fixture whose overlap region is scored against Chromium, and the oracle extended to assert the overlap pixel rather than only the command alphas. CLOSED by SP-8 on 2026-11-12: paint now records a clean faded box as a contiguous [Start,End) group carrying its own OwnOpacity and withholds that fraction from every member command (internal/paint/builder_box.go, internal/paint/list.go); the tile raster renders the range into a pooled, tile-sized scratch, fades it exactly once (fadePixels) and blits it down (compositeGroup in internal/raster/tile.go), recursing into nested child groups. Deterministic pixel oracle TestGroupOpacityOverlapComposite reads non-overlap (191,191,255) and overlap (158,158,255) within rounding tolerance - exactly the value the defect produced as (143,143,255); TestGroupOpacityCountedOncePerElement proves the fade applies once per element across span/anon/anondiv/quarter/nested/tableAnon/pseudoOwn. Parity fixture css-features/18-group-opacity-overlap.html scored against Chromium at 98.37% PASS (worst_region_iou 1.0, no blank bands), corpus 107/107 (100.0%), average 96.43%, known gaps unchanged at 4 fixtures / 6 bands; go test -race on paint/raster and the full matrix (build, vet, ./..., archtest, gate with ScratchAllocs 0) are green. Three mutants prove each gate is live: disabling the offscreen composite (raster overlap RED), folding the fade into effective as well as the group (builder CountedOncePerElement RED on all 7 shapes), and forcing isCleanFadedGroup to true (TestFadedBoxWithZDescendantIsNotGrouped RED). SCOPE LIMITATION, not reopened: a faded box with a z-index>0 descendant is NOT a clean group (its members are not contiguous after SortStable), so it stays on the unchanged per-command path and can still double-darken when it also self-overlaps; rare, tracked as a known limitation.

summary: Text-run and inline-fragment boxes repaint their generating element's background, so a translucent block background is composited again wherever a word sits.
evidence: GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001 - measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while reviewing TASK-044 §5.10, which names the same shape as out of scope. `cmd/dump-paint` on a 300x60 block with `background:rgb(200,0,0)` and the text `one two three four` emits the block fill `(0,0,300,60)` once and then one more fill per word box: `(0,0,24,18) (23,0,28,18) (27,0,52,18) (51,0,56,18) (55,0,88,18) (87,0,92,18) (91,0,118,18)`. With an opaque background the duplication is invisible (red over red), so it was never a paint-correctness bug until opacity/translucency arrived: with `background:rgba(200,0,0,0.5)` the same document renders (213,63,63) inside a word box against (227,127,127) elsewhere in the block, and Chromium renders (227,127,127) uniformly at all three sampled points - i.e. Goosie applies the element's own 0.5 alpha twice wherever a text fragment covers it. Inline *fragmenting* (one background per line fragment of an inline box) is correct CSS; what is wrong is a **block** element's background being re-emitted by the text runs layout splices under it, which is the same verbatim style copy that made group opacity double-count (`style.inheritStyle: cs := *parent`). TASK-044 deliberately kept translucent backgrounds out of faded groups in fixture 13 so the corpus would not score this. What closing needs: the fragment fills to carry the fragment's own background only, an oracle at the style->paint boundary asserting one background per box per line, and a scored fixture with a translucent block background over text. CORRECTION by the integrator, 2026-10-26: the fill list above first said six duplicate run fills; the true number is **seven** - `(91,0,118,18)` for the fourth word was left out of my own transcription. TASK-048's mutation-A log quotes all eight fills (one box + seven runs) and is the citation for the corrected list.  CLOSED by TASK-048, merged in 271238a, re-measured by the integrator on this host before the merge: `cmd/dump-paint` on the same document emits exactly 1 fill of `1677721728` after the fix against 8 on main; the pixel oracle `TestTranslucentBlockBackgroundCompositesOnce` reads (227,127,127) where main read (213,63,63); mutations A (predicate always true: rc 1, 12 FAIL headers, 26 assertion lines), B (always false: rc 1, 5/4, killing exactly the two inline controls) and C (inverted sign: rc 1, 15/29) all die, and TASK-044/046's oracles stay green under A (rc 0, 9 PASS), so the red cannot be re-attributed to the group-opacity plan. Parity 88/88 (100.0%), average 96.17%, new fixture `css-features/14-inline-background-repaint.html` 94.19% PASS, floor 87->88, `go test -count=1 -race ./...` clean across 42 packages. What this entry does NOT close, registered as its own defects on the same day of measurement: GOOSIE-ANONBG-001 (an anonymous block box re-composites its parent's gradient or background-image), GOOSIE-SHADOWRUN-001 (a box-shadow declaration emits once per text run), and GOOSIE-INLINEBORDER-001 (an inline element's border is never emitted). LIVE READ, sweep 7 (build `741fdd37`) 2026-10-26: this fix has **no measurable footprint on the 100-site corpus** and that is disclosed rather than smoothed over. Of 94 compared rows, 84 have byte-identical `ink_goosie` against sweep 6 and no row shows the fix's signature (a colour-only change with stable ink) above the capture noise; the one flip attributable to code is https://www.24h.com.vn/ MISSING_REGIONS -> LOW_COVERAGE with its blank reference bands going 1/5 -> 0/4 and `pct_exact` +9.93 — an improvement that exposes a pre-existing coverage gap (Chromium 628,362 ink px vs Goosie 269,480) rather than a new defect. The other five flips are capture state or network: de.wikipedia and zh.wikipedia flip with Goosie's ink identical to the byte while Chromium's ink moves +42% / -0.5%, nld.com.vn flips on Chromium ink +391% with Goosie -0.1%, bestbuy.com is a Chromium-side TimeoutError (GOOSIE-LIVE-007), walmart.com is the non-reproducibility registered as GOOSIE-LIVE-009. Fixture 14 and the three mutations stay the accepted evidence for this closure.

summary: `visibility: collapse` is treated as `hidden`, so a table row or column that should collapse keeps its box and its share of the table grid.
evidence: GOOSIE-COLLAPSE-001 - registered from TASK-044 §5.9, which ships the simplification and says so in the code comment at `internal/paint/builder_box.go` ("`collapse` is treated as hidden here; table-part collapse is out of scope"). Per CSS 2.1 / UI, `collapse` on a row, rowgroup or column removes it from the table's width/height distribution (adjacent borders and half-borders merge), which is observably different from `hidden`; a box that only stops painting still occupies its cells. **Integrator note on evidence quality: not measured by me** - no Chromium anchor for a collapsed row exists in this repo and no oracle asserts either behaviour, so the size of the gap is unquantified. Priority P3 for that reason, not because the difference is small. What closing needs: a Chromium-measured collapsed-row fixture, then a decision on whether to implement table-part collapse or record it as out of scope for the release with the roadmap item named.

summary: `content-visibility: auto` resolves to no behaviour: only the literal `hidden` is consulted in layout and paint, so `auto` falls through to normal painting and sizing.
evidence: GOOSIE-CONTENTVIS-001 - registered while reviewing TASK-044 §5.9, which leaves the property alone deliberately. Scope of the claim, narrowed after checking the code: the property is **not** inert. `internal/style/style.go:2139` stores it, `DefaultStyle()` gives `visible` at :689, and there are real consumers - `internal/layout/block.go:167` and :2436 (`hidden` skips contents and can size from `ContainIntrinsicHeight`) and `internal/paint/builder_box.go:37` (`hidden` stops the subtree walk) - plus tests `test/style/content_visibility_test.go:TestContentVisibilityProperties`, `TestContentVisibilitySingleIntrinsicSize` and `test/layout/anchor_test.go:TestContentVisibilityHiddenLayoutSizing`. What is missing is `auto`: every comparison in the tree is `== "hidden"`, so the value the cascade stores for `auto` is read nowhere and a document using `content-visibility: auto` behaves as if it said `visible`. **Correction kept on the record: the first draft of this entry, written before the grep above, said the field had no consumer and no test. That was false and is withdrawn here rather than quietly edited away.** Not measured against Chromium on this host, so no claim is made about which part of the `auto` contract (skipped rendering, contain-intrinsic-size swap, finding-in-page) matters most. What closing needs: a Chromium anchor for `auto` on a long page, then either the behaviour or an explicit scope statement in the roadmap.

summary: An anonymous block box re-composites its generating block’s gradient or background-image, because `style.AnonymousBlockStyle` zeroes only `BackgroundColor` while `AnonymousTableStyle` zeroes all four background layers.
evidence: GOOSIE-ANONBG-001 - found by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while checking whether TASK-048’s new predicate (`internal/paint/builder_box.go:29 fragmentOwnsBackground`) left a hole at `obj.Node == nil -> true`, which is exactly the branch an anonymous block takes. Measured on `/tmp/t48-check/anon-grad.html` (a 300x76 block with `background:linear-gradient(rgba(200,0,0,.5),rgba(200,0,0,.5))` holding raw text plus a block sibling, so `cmd/dump-layout` shows anonymous boxes ID=11 (0,0,300,18) and ID=12 (0,38,300,18)), 400x120 DPR 1, counts over the box area: Chromium 13,370 px (227,127,127) + 8,595 px (228,127,127) and no doubled colour at all; main 12,000 px (227,127,127) + 8,190 px (213,63,63) doubled + 1,777 px (206,31,31) tripled; after TASK-048 12,000 px (227,127,127) + 10,026 px (213,63,63). The tripled colour disappears because it came from text runs (BR-198); the doubled band survives because it comes from the anonymous boxes, which own no background colour to zero — style.go:450 clears `BackgroundColor` only, while :635-642 (table) clears `BackgroundColor`, `BackgroundImage`, `BackgroundGradient` and `BackgroundRadialGradient`. So the mechanism TASK-048 added is right and the style layer is the one that is inconsistent. The solid-colour path is provably unreachable for anonymous boxes: `anon-bg.html` emits exactly one fill of `1677721728` post-fix against 8 on main, and dump-paint shows no anonymous-box-width fill in either build. Why the corpus does not catch it: fixture 13 keeps gradients out of translucent groups and fixture 14 uses a solid background. What closing needs: mirror :636-642 into `AnonymousBlockStyle` (or gate gradient/image paints on the same owner test in the builder), a fixture whose gradient band sits behind raw text beside a block sibling, and an oracle asserting one gradient fill per element. Not fixed here; needs a task. CLOSURE MEASURED BY THE INTEGRATOR on main 1f0ba78, 2026-10-26, not taken from the branch: `cmd/goosie-headless` 400x120 DPR 1 on /tmp/t48-check/anon-grad.html, counted over the block's 300x76 area (22,800 px): 0 px of the twice-composited (213,63,63) (10,026 before) and 22,026 px of (227,127,127), against Chromium's 21,965 (13,370 exact + 8,595 of its (228,127,127) rounding) - the residue is alpha rounding, not a second composite. Display list: exactly one gradient rect (0,0,300,76) per declaring element, the anonymous bands contribute none; under mutation A the same oracle names the extra rects verbatim `(0,0,300,18)` and `(0,38,300,56)` (13 FAIL headers / 17 lines, re-run by me). Mutation C (collapse moved into `fragmentOwnsBackground`) kills only test/style - 6 headers / 5 lines, re-run by me - which is the disclosed limit: the paint oracles are result-accurate, the style oracle is the stage-accurate one. Mutation B (over-collapse) is branch-reported (12/21 plus 8/10) and I did not re-measure it. Fixture css-features/15-anonymous-block-gradient-once.html scores 95.88% PASS (worst_region_iou=0.9994, coverage_ratio=0.9931, blank_regions=0/0) and 72.98% FAIL when re-rendered with the pre-fix binary `python3 testdata/parity.py --render --binary /tmp/t049-work/goosie-pre` -> 88/89, average 95.91%, rc 1; the corpus floor MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES goes 88 -> 89 on this fixture alone. summary: An inline element’s border is never painted at all: `paintBorders` sits behind a non-inline test, so inline boxes lose their borders instead of fragmenting them per line.
evidence: GOOSIE-INLINEBORDER-001 - reported by TASK-048 §6.1 and re-measured independently by the integrator on 2026-10-26 on my own document `/tmp/t48-res/inlineborder.html` (`div{width:300px;height:60px;margin:10px;background:rgba(200,0,0,.5)}` with `span{border:3px solid rgba(0,0,200,.5)}` around "two"). `cmd/dump-paint` emits **0** BORDER commands on main and **0** on the TASK-048 branch — the only BORDER in the engine’s output for a block border test appears for the block itself (`BORDER rect=(0,0,306,66)` in TASK-048’s §6.1 dump), never for an inline. Chromium paints the span’s border box: over my measured region Chromium holds 198 px of (113,63,163) — exactly `rgba(0,0,200,.5)` composited once over the block tint (227,127,127) — and Goosie holds none of that colour anywhere; Goosie’s only extra colours in the region are glyph antialiasing (125,70,70 / 68,38,38 / 191,107,107). Root is the same test that protects borders from the duplication in GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001: `paintBoxDecoration` runs `paintBorders` only when `computed.Display != style.DisplayInline`, so text runs (inline) cannot re-emit the element’s border — which is why no border duplication exists to register — but an inline element’s own border is dropped rather than fragmented one box per line, as CSS fragmentation requires. Blast radius: any page that draws a rule or a chip outline with `border` on an inline element (including `<a>`/`<abbr>`/`<code>` styling) loses it silently; invisible to the corpus because no fixture puts a border on an inline box. What closing needs: emit one border per inline fragment of an inline element (left/right strips only at the true start/end of the run, per css-text-decor L3 §4.6 analogue), an oracle counting BORDER commands per fragment, and a scored fixture. Needs a task. CLOSURE (SP-7, 2026-11-12): layout records per-line border-box fragments on Object.InlineFragments (internal/layout/inline.go finalizeInlineFragments, captured under the generating inline element by DOM parent in the positioning loop; inline borders are resolved at Block entry because inlineInto first runs inside the Block pass); paint emits one CmdBorder per fragment with top/bottom on every fragment and the inline-start/inline-end edges only on the first/last (internal/paint/builder_borders.go paintBorderFragment, builder_box.go paintBoxDecoration). Oracles: test/layout/inline_border_fragment_test.go (fragment count/order/edge expansion) and test/paint/inline_border_fragment_test.go (one border per fragment, start/end mask). Three mutants killed: M1 suppress guard, M2 four-edge-per-fragment, M3 union-rect-only. Fixture borders/04-inline-fragment.html scores 98.86% PASS with no blank band, MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES 105 -> 106, the prior 105 fixtures byte-identical, corpus gaps unchanged 4 fixtures / 6 bands. Deferred (spec section 8): inline outline, border-image and border-radius on fragments, RTL pixel sign-off.

summary: A live-sweep row is not reproducible even when the binary is bit-identical: what a page’s row records depends on how far that page’s own scripts got at capture time, so the same URL on the same engine yields a 4,368 px document in one sweep and a 34,795 px one in the next.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-009 - measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while attributing sweep 7 (`docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-26T0011Z-741fdd37`, build source `741fdd37`) against sweep 6 (`2026-10-25T2212Z-4302e3cb`, build source `9754fda4`). The engine side is provably deterministic: three consecutive `./bin/goosie -backend headless -width 1280 -height 1024 -dpr 1 -screenshot -url https://www.walmart.com/` runs on this host produced **one** PNG hash (`6472fedefe08…`, 500,177 B) and **one** ink count (1,138,344 non-white px) with rc 0 and the same stderr each time. Yet walmart’s row says `ink_goosie` 1,077,200 with `doc_height` 4,368 in sweep 6 and 519,333 with `doc_height` 34,795 in sweep 7 — an 8× document height and a 52% ink swing on a URL whose HTML is byte-stable (three `curl` fetches: 450,325 B, sha256 prefix `14b086e65f377ad7`, identical). The page’s own script state, not the engine and not the HTML, is what moved. Scale of it, from the same two sweeps: **84 of 94** compared rows have byte-identical `ink_goosie` across two different builds, and every row where both `ink_goosie` and `ink_chromium` are identical also has `pct_exact` delta **exactly 0.00** (apnews.com, datatracker.ietf.org, doc.rust-lang.org/book and std, docs.kernel.org, docs.python.org ×3, en.wikipedia ×3 …) — so the metric is reproducible and the noise is entirely in what the reference and the page contribute at capture time. The movers confirm the direction: nld.com.vn `pct_exact` −27.39 with `ink_goosie` −0.1% and `ink_chromium` **+391%**; de.wikipedia −6.08 with ink Goosie identical and Chromium +42%; zingnews `ink_goosie` **+68.8%** (an engine change that only *removes* fills cannot add ink, so this is page state); two of six label flips (de/zh.wikipedia) happen with Goosie’s ink identical to the byte. Consequence for how a sweep may be read: a label flip or a `pct_exact` move is an engine result only when the engine’s own numbers moved too — which is why sweep 7 attributes exactly **one** of its six flips to code (see GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001’s note) and the rest to capture state. Not the same defect: GOOSIE-LIVE-004 (a row can read OK while the pixels are nowhere near each other), GOOSIE-LIVE-007 (FETCH_FAILED is decided on Chromium’s side — sweep 7 proves it again with bestbuy.com’s `TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 30000ms`, where Goosie never got a turn), GOOSIE-LIVE-008 (report naming). What closing needs: pin the page state the row is allowed to depend on (wait for network idle plus a settled script-error count, or capture `doc_height` twice and refuse to score an unstable page), and record which of the two the row was taken with. Needs a task. Sweep 7 also brought its own repeated-pass noise floor back tighter than sweep 5/6 had it: 12 sites, 10 comparable, max |delta_pct_exact| **0.67**, max |delta_coverage| 0.077, **0** label flips. Read together that is the point of this entry - the spread on *static* pages is well under a point, while the pages that moved between sweeps moved 6 to 27 points, and every one of those movers has a reference- or script-side number that moved with it. A sweep's own repeated pass therefore cannot detect the instability this entry describes: it re-renders the same pages inside one capture window, where the page state is already fixed.

summary: The one non-test caller of the unchecked paint entry point is a shipped diagnostic: `cmd/dump-paint` paints geometry the engine refused to validate, and no test covers any `cmd/dump-*` binary at all.
evidence: GOOSIE-DIAGPAINT-001 - found by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while using `cmd/dump-paint` as a probe for TASK-048. Scope of the claim, measured rather than assumed: a repo-wide search for `Session.Paint(` and `PaintChecked(` outside tests yields 20 shipped call sites, 19 of them `PaintChecked` and exactly one raw `Paint(1)` - `cmd/dump-paint/main.go:28`. Everything the product runs (`cmd/goosie/*`, `cmd/goosie-headless`) is on the checked path, so this is not a user-facing bypass; it is a diagnostic an operator points at a file. Why it still matters: `AGENTS.md` "Untrusted Input" states binaries that touch untrusted input must call `Session.PaintChecked`, never `Paint`, and this binary reads an HTML file the operator supplies - which is untrusted input by that definition - and it is also the tool the QA registry now cites as evidence in catalog rows (BR-198 quotes its fill list, GOOSIE-VIS-001 and TASK-048 do the same), so a probe that skips the geometry gate can show commands a shipped build would never emit. The guard gap is separately real: `test/entrypoints/limits_test.go` builds and runs only `goosie-headless` and `goosie` (its six tests: invalid viewport, oversized document, valid document, screenshot invalid viewport, screenshot valid, oversized input) - searching the whole `test/` tree for `cmd/dump-paint` finds only two prose comments in `test/paint/inline_background_repaint_test.go:14,225`, no test. What closing needs: `dump-paint` (and a check over the other `cmd/dump-*`/`cmd/debug-*` binaries) to take `PaintChecked` and print the refusal on stderr with a non-zero rc, plus a source-level or process-level guard so a future diagnostic cannot silently re-add the unchecked call. Not measured: whether any of the other diagnostics admit input before parsing; this entry does not claim they do not. SECOND DEFECT OF THE SAME TOOL, measured 2026-10-26 while validating TASK-049: `cmd/dump-paint` prints only FILL, BORDER and TEXT lines, so it cannot see `CmdGradient`, `CmdRadialGradient` or `CmdImage` at all. That blind spot is why the anonymous-block gradient re-emission - three gradient rects `(0,0,300,76) (0,0,300,18) (0,38,300,56)` where Chromium has one - looked like nothing in the dump: TASK-049 had to read the display list through `paint.Builder` inside a Go test to see it (its 1.2). Registry rows written before this note (BR-198, GOOSIE-VIS-001) quote dump-paint fill lists as if they were the whole list; they are a projection. Closing this entry must therefore do two things, not one: switch the binary to `PaintChecked` AND print every command kind the tile path honours, otherwise the next gradient or image defect is again invisible to the only diagnostic an operator runs.

summary: A quoted `url("…")` whose payload contains `)` is cut at the first `)`, so inline-SVG backgrounds that use `rgb()`/`rgba()` colours lose the layer entirely while Chromium paints them; the computed value itself is wrong, not just the pixels.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSURLPAREN-001 - found by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while checking a claim TASK-049 handed up ("Goosie never paints background-image"). That claim is FALSIFIED, and the real defect is narrower: measured with /tmp/bgimg-probe/variants5.html (four 100x20 bands, `cmd/goosie-headless` 120x90 DPR 1 against a Playwright capture of the same file), counting exact (0,0,255) px per band - Chromium paints ALL FOUR forms at 2,000 px; Goosie paints the two forms whose SVG carries a `%230000ff` colour at 2,000 px each and the two forms whose SVG carries `fill='rgb(0,0,255)'` at 0 px. Base64 forms paint too (svg;base64 Goosie 1,493 vs Chromium 1,455; png;base64 Goosie 1,458 vs Chromium 1,392 - the small deltas are tile-repeat seam rounding, a separate question). The corpus proves the same from the other side: colors/03-opacity.html carries an inline SVG background written with `%23ccc` and paints 27,314 px of (204,204,204) in Goosie against Chromium's 28,502, which is why no fixture is red today. MECHANISM, located by reading the computed value rather than guessing it: a throwaway cascade probe (run 2026-10-26, then deleted) printed `style.ComputedStyle.BackgroundImage` for each form - for the working form it is the full 140-char URI, for the broken one it is `data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='20' height='20'><rect width='20' height='20' fill='rgb(0,0,255` at 133 chars, i.e. the string STOPS at the first `)`. So the cut is in the *value re-scan*, not in the tokenizer: `internal/css/parser.go:1178,1739` already honour 4.3.9 (a quote inside `url(…)` is not a string start), but `internal/style/style.go:4050 extractBackgroundURL` re-extracts the payload with `strings.IndexByte(rest, ')')` (`:4054`) and only strips the quotes *after* that cut (`:4059`), so `url("…rgb(0,0,255)…")` comes back as `"…rgb(0,0,255` - exactly the 133 chars the probe printed. Searching `internal/` for that pattern found FIVE extraction sites: `style.go:4054`; `internal/css/border_image.go:57 borderImageURL`; `internal/engine/limits.go:786 absolutizeCSSURLs`, which cuts and then re-emits the tail as new text, so a fetched sheet's quoted data URI is truncated *and* rewritten; `internal/engine/imports.go:101 importRef`; and `internal/engine/engine.go:419`, which is already quote-aware (`:413-419`) and is the reference for what the shared scanner must do. Only the first is proven by pixels today; TASK-050 is written against all five, and `internal/engine/limits.go:743 decodeDataImageURL` then faithfully percent-unescapes a URI that is no longer valid XML, so `imgdec.DecodeSVGAt` (`internal/engine/engine.go:874`) fails and `obj.BgImage` is never set (`:878`). Note `internal/paint/builder_background.go:72` DOES read `obj.BgImage`, so the paint layer is not the gap; TASK-049 named the wrong layer. Blast radius: `rgb()`/`rgba()` inside an inline SVG is one of the two idioms sites actually write (the other is `%23` hex, which works), so placeholder art, chevrons and gradient-on-SVG backgrounds vanish silently - and unlike a refused document this prints no diagnostic anywhere. What closing needs: the tokenizer must consume a quoted url up to its terminating quote (and reject unbalanced parens only in the unquoted form), an oracle asserting `BackgroundImage` byte-for-byte for a payload containing `)`, `(`, `%`, `#` and `'`, plus a scored fixture whose SVG background uses `rgba()`; and the falsified upstream claim should be corrected in TASK-049 rather than left standing. Priority note: this adds a sixth open P0/P1 entry, which the rc-sweep gate reads - it belongs at P1 because a shipped document's computed style is provably wrong, not because one layer is prettier. RE-MEASURED on main a5c5424 the same day, independently of the first probe: `cmd/goosie-headless -in /tmp/bgimg-probe/variants5.html -width 120 -height 90 -dpr 1` counts (0,0,255) px per band `[2000, 2000, 0, 0]`, while a Playwright capture of the identical file counts `[2000, 2000, 2000, 2000]` and keeps the whole payload in the computed value (lengths 147/142/150/145). So the discriminator is a `)` in the payload - not `;utf8`, not quoting: k1 (unquoted, `%230000ff`) paints and k3 (unquoted, `rgb(0,0,255)`) does not. Owner is now TASK-050 (spec `docs/tasks/TASK-050-CSS-URL-PAREN.md`, implementer dispatched 2026-10-26). CLOSED 2026-10-26 by TASK-050, merged at 6edb7e3 (implementation f171d6c, registration 8f58aa8), cases BR-211/BR-212. Fix: one shared scanner `internal/css/url.go` (`ScanURL`/`ScanURLAt`/`IndexURL`) that follows CSS Syntax L3 4.3.9 - a quoted payload runs to its matching quote and the token ends at the following `)`; an unquoted payload is read with balanced-paren depth - replaces the flat cut at SIX sites, not five: the five listed above plus `ParseBorderImageShorthand` in `internal/css/border_image.go`, found during the audit because it rejoined `strings.Fields` tokens around a quote-blind `strings.Contains(")")` and truncated a shorthand border-image the same way. Re-measured by the integrator on this host after the merge: (a) the doc's page /tmp/bgimg-probe/variants5.html, 120x90 DPR 1 - Goosie before [2000,2000,0,0], after [2000,2000,2000,2000], Chromium [2000,2000,2000,2000]; (b) new eight-band fixture testdata/render/css-features/16-url-paren-data-image.html scored against a fresh Playwright capture - 98.69% PASS (IoU 1.0, coverage 0.997295) after, 74.69% FAIL (IoU 0.683531, coverage 0.517161) on main; exact (0,0,255) px 230,400 in Chromium and after, 115,200 before; (c) whole corpus 91/91 (100.0%), average 96.21%, known gaps 5 fixtures / 10 bands unchanged, rc 0 after; 90/91, average 95.95%, rc 1 on main. Behaviour proof: eight mutants, each red and each restored to rc 0 - M01 revert extractBackgroundURL (5 tests die), M02 quote-blind scanner (8), M03 paren-blind scanner (6), M04 fail-open unterminated quote (7), M05 border-image longhand (2), M06 absolutizeCSSURLs (1), M07 importRef (1), M08 font (1). Deliberate limits, not hidden: a backslash escape inside a quoted payload still drops the declaration (registered separately as GOOSIE-CSSURLESCAPE-001), and unquoted payloads carrying a literal quote or `(` are painted although Chromium treats them as bad-url - pre-existing leniency, now pinned explicitly at BR-211; the parity fixture only uses forms Chromium itself accepts. `docs/tasks/TASK-050-CSS-URL-PAREN.md` records the spec, the audit table and these measurements.

summary: HTML IDL attribute reflection is a per-property patchwork with no element prototypes behind it: `className` neither reads nor writes the `class` attribute (a script setting it changes nothing in the DOM or the render), while `id` and `input.value` do; `Object.getPrototypeOf(el) === Object.prototype`, and entire interfaces are absent — all 21 measured `img` properties and `a.href`/`hostname`/`target`/`rel` are `undefined` even though the attributes are there.
evidence:
Measured by the integrator on main 89d7a07 with a throwaway `package js_test` probe (`domtest.Parse` + `newRuntime` at URL `https://example.test/docs/page.html` + `r.Run`, then deleted). `<div id=d class=c0>`: `d.className='k'` leaves `d.getAttribute('class')` at **`c0`**, and the reverse direction is missing too — `createElement('div').setAttribute('class','z')` then reading `.className` gives **`''`**. So the assignment creates an own JS property that the DOM and the cascade never read: a script that sets `className` changes nothing about rendering, silently. `id` and `input.value` DO write through (`id='q2'` → `getAttribute('id')=='q2'` and `getElementById('q2')` resolves; `value='zz'` → attribute `zz`), which is exactly what a per-property patchwork looks like: `test/js/dataset_test.go`-style coverage exists where a task needed it, and `internal/js` grew no element interfaces. `Object.getPrototypeOf(divElement) === Object.prototype` — there is no `HTMLElement` (or `HTMLAnchorElement` / `HTMLImageElement`) prototype, so nothing is inherited and `el instanceof HTMLDivElement` is unimplementable today.
The same probe enumerated the damage on two element classes. `a` (`href="/p?q=1"`): `href`, `hostname`, `target`, `rel` are all `typeof undefined` while `getAttribute('href')` returns `/p?q=1` — so no absolute-URL resolution happens for links read from script. `img` (`src=x.png width=10`): **every** IDL attribute measured is undefined — `src`, `currentSrc`, `width`, `height`, `naturalWidth`, `naturalHeight`, `complete`, `loading`, `decoding`, `alt`, `srcset`, `sizes`, `x`, `y`, `hspace`, `vspace`, `border`, `name`, `useMap`, `isMap`, `longDesc`, `decode` (21 forms) — while `getAttribute('src')`/`('width')` return `x.png`/`10`. `tagName` on `createElement('img')` is correctly `IMG`, so the element exists; only the interface is absent.
RELATION TO OTHER IDS: this is the general case of `GOOSIE-IMAGE-001` (missing `Image` constructor *and* propertyless img elements) and of the `GOOSIE-IDLREFLECT-001` report the TASK-047 agent handed up, whose `className` half my table above confirms. Their ids converge on this one entry rather than duplicating it. Not claimed: how many live sites break on this — vnexpress's remaining error after TASK-047 is `Image is not defined`, which is the constructor face, and the sweep after each merge is what answers the blast radius (GOOSIE-LIVE-001).
WHAT CLOSING NEEDS: an `HTMLElement` prototype (plus the per-interface prototypes the IDL defines) whose properties are real accessors reading and writing attributes, installed once on the element prototypes rather than per node; a reflection table per element class with the IDL's rules honoured — `long`/`unsigned long` with default values, boolean reflection (`disabled`, `hidden`), reflected DOMString with case rules (`img.alt`) and limited-to-known-values (`loading`, `decoding`), URL reflection resolving against the document base with the `href` getter returning the absolute URL — and the same rules applied to the interfaces sites actually touch first (`a`, `img`, `link`, `form`, `input`, `button`, `iframe`, `script`, `canvas`). Spec order matters: `internal/js` may not import `internal/style` (`internal/archtest/rules.go:20-44` allows `internal/dom` and `internal/media` only), so URL resolution must come from something `js` is already allowed to use, or the table gets edited deliberately, the way TASK-051 justifies adding `internal/css`. Sequenced as TASK-052 behind TASK-047 and TASK-051 because all three edit `internal/js/js.go`.
PARTIAL, measured 2026-10-26 on merge 6668ad8: TASK-052 landed the general mechanism this id asked for - a real prototype chain (BR-236), reflected DOMString/boolean/unsigned-long/enumerated/URL accessors (BR-237..242), live classList/attributes/style (BR-241), and `className` writes that reach the cascade rather than a dead own property (BR-247). `Object.getPrototypeOf(div)` is now `HTMLDivElement.prototype` and the anchor/image/input interfaces answer. REMAINING SCOPE (why this id stays open): the per-interface reflection tables cover only `HTMLAnchorElement`, `HTMLImageElement` and `HTMLInputElement` (`internal/js/element_interfaces.go:167-173` dispatches to `installAnchorInterface`/`installImageInterface`/`installInputInterface`); the other prototypes exist but carry no class-specific accessors, so `link.href`, `form.action/method`, `button.type/value`, `iframe.src`, `script.src/async/defer`, `canvas.width/height` and their siblings still read `undefined` while the attributes are present. Closing this id now would record the general case as done when it is done for three interfaces out of the tag list at `internal/js/element_interfaces.go:125-136`. No oracle asserts the missing per-tag tables yet.
CLOSED 2026-11-02 (BR-262, commit 9027402): the per-interface tables named in REMAINING SCOPE now answer — form.action/method, button.type/value/disabled, iframe.src, script.src/async/defer, canvas.width/height were already installed, and HTMLLinkElement gained href (URL-resolved), rel, as, media, hreflang, type, sizes, integrity, imageSrcset/imageSizes, crossOrigin and disabled. crossOrigin now shares installCrossOriginReflection with image, so the nullable-enum semantics cannot drift. summary: A quoted `url("…\"…")` payload that contains a backslash escape is dropped entirely - Chromium unescapes it and paints the image, Goosie paints nothing. The shared scanner deliberately fails closed on a backslash inside the quoted payload.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSURLESCAPE-001 - found while auditing TASK-050's own fix on 2026-10-26. The first draft of `internal/css/url.go` justified returning ok=false on a backslash by calling the token "a bad string per 4.3.9"; that was WRONG - CSS Syntax L3 section 4.3.9 makes a backslash a legal escape, and the pre-TASK-050 readers also failed on the form, so this is a pre-existing gap that the fix neither created nor closed, now stated instead of mislabelled. Measured by the integrator on this host with /tmp/t50/esc.html (a 40x20 div whose background is a quoted SVG data URI whose fill attribute is written with escaped quotes, DPR 1, exact (0,0,255) px): Chromium 800 px; Goosie 0 px before TASK-050 and 0 px after the merge at 6edb7e3. Impact is narrower than GOOSIE-CSSURLPAREN-001 because consumers rarely escape quotes in data URIs (they usually alternate quoting or percent-encode), but a declaration that renders in every other browser disappears here with no diagnostic. What closing needs: decode CSS escapes inside a quoted URL payload (`\"` -> `"`, hex escapes per 4.3.9) before handing the payload to the resolver, keep the fail-closed behaviour only for genuinely unterminated tokens, add unit cases for escaped quote/backslash/hex escape, and extend the reader tests so the font/@import/border-image paths are covered too. Priority P2: one value per document, no crash, no wrong bytes - it just fails to paint. CLOSED by 74d424c6 (2026-11-12, BR-269). The scanner now consumes every `\X` pair while it reads the payload, so `\"` cannot close a quoted token, `\\` cannot leave the next quote stray, and in the unquoted form `\(` and `\)` cannot move the paren depth - `url(a\)b.png)` is one token for the URL `a)b.png` instead of a token cut at the escaped ')' that strands `b.png)`. Fail-closed narrows to the shapes that genuinely never end: an unterminated quoted payload (`url("abc`) and parentheses that never balance. Two roles had to be separated because absolutizeCSSURLs re-emits the payload into stylesheet text: `URLToken.Payload` keeps the source spelling - decoding there would rewrite `url("a\"b")` into the broken `url("a"b")` - and every consumer that resolves, fetches or matches takes the URL from the new exported `css.URLPayload` = `DecodeEscapes`: extractBackgroundURL (background-image and mask-image/-webkit-mask-image, one reader for both), borderImageURL, extractFontURL and importRef (plus `unquote` for the `@import "..."` form). Expectations were measured on 2026-11-12 at two levels rather than recalled from spec. getComputedStyle: `url("a\41 b.png")` -> `aAb.png`, `url(a\)b.png)` -> `a)b.png`, `url("a\ b.png")` -> `a b.png`, which Chromium then writes back percent-encoded. The request log of a real HTTP server for a sheet at /sub.css: `url("i\63 on.png")` and `url("ic\6fn.png")` both fetch /icon.png (a hex escape stops at the first non-hex byte, so the second needs no terminator), `url("br\"dr.png")` fetches /br"dr.png, `url(no\2dsuch.png)` fetches /no-such.png, `url("a\ b.png")` fetches /a b.png, `@import url("b\42 .css")` fetches /bB.css and applies it (.imp takes rgb(0, 0, 255)), `@font-face src:url("fo\6f.ttf")` fetches /foo.ttf, and all five escaped @import spellings - `url("su\62.css")`, `"su\62.css"`, `url(su\62.css)`, `url('su\62.css')`, `url("su\62\2e css")` - fetch and apply /sub.css. Resolving the decoded form exposed a hazard the old code could not reach: net/url percent-encodes quotes, spaces and backslashes but leaves `(`/`)` raw in a path, so a rewritten unquoted reference could emit sheet text the next scan cuts early; emitURLRef/needsURLQuote re-emit with the source's own quote and promote an unquoted token to a quoted one when the absolute URL carries a paren, and that property is pinned by re-scanning the emitted sheet (ScanURL + URLPayload) rather than by comparing strings. Sixteen oracles tagged `// qc:BR-269` on five layers: internal/css/url_test.go (2: payload decode + sheet text kept intact, plus two rows of the old Rule-3 table corrected because they pinned this defect's wrong contract), test/css/url_escape_test.go (3: a 16-row ParseBorderImageSource table carrying the three escaped-quote spellings of one SVG data URI, a 4-row shorthand table, and the BorderImage struct receiving source + `7 fill`), test/style/url_escape_test.go (4: background 8 rows, the three spellings of one URI, mask-image + -webkit-mask-image, the shorthand after an escaped payload), internal/engine/url_escape_test.go (6: extractFontURL, collectFontJobs -> https://e/x/foo.woff2, a 12-row importRef covering the @import spellings and the still-rejected `print` media, absolutizeCSSURLs round-trip with kept refs byte for byte, expandCSSImports with both layers escaped), test/engine/url_escape_test.go (1: four spellings attach the background to the arena - before the fix BgImage was nil). Two mutations discriminate: stubbing DecodeEscapes to `return s` kills the three escaped cases while the percent-encoded control stays green, and test/style fails with the literal message MaskImage = "m\41 sk.png", want mAsk.png; a binary built from the pre-fix tree (git worktree at HEAD) scores the new fixture 95.83% FAIL (worst_region_iou 0.0, coverage_ratio 0.8436, blank bands 2/0, rows (88,127)+(138,177)) with 0 blue px against Chromium's 14,400 and the fixed build's 14,400. Fixture css-features/20-url-escaped-quote-data-image.html scores 98.834% PASS (worst_region_iou 0.9932, coverage_ratio 0.985, blank bands 0/0); its third control is `\22` with NO terminator - the hex read grabs all six digits, giving U+2240 and a broken URI, so both engines must paint white, and that was measured. summary: `Runtime.CheckIntersections` calls `entry.target.Export()` while holding `Runtime.mu`; exporting a node wrapper invokes its enumerable `shadowRoot`/`parentNode` getters, which call back into the runtime and try to take the same non-reentrant mutex, so any page that registers an IntersectionObserver deadlocks `NewSession` forever - the browser never finishes loading and a screenshot run is killed at its 120 s harness timeout.
evidence: GOOSIE-IOEXPORT-001 - found 2026-10-26 while comparing live sweep #9 (report docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-26T0427Z-b46d4d51.json) against sweep #8: two pages that sweep #8 scored (getbootstrap.com LOW_COVERAGE in 0.54 s; vietnamnet.vn LOW_COVERAGE in 2.21 s) became GOOSIE_TIMEOUT at exactly 120.01 s, and the same run's structure call also timed out. MINIMAL REPRO: /tmp/t50-iohang.html is a 100x100 blue div plus `new IntersectionObserver(function(es){document.title='io '+es.length}).observe(document.getElementById('x'))`; /tmp/t50-control.html is the same page without the script. With `-backend headless -width 200 -height 150 -dpr 1 -screenshot`, the control renders in 0.18 s (rc 0) and the observer page does not finish in 20 s on the merged build b46d4d5, nor in 15 s on a5c54245 (the sweep-8 source) nor on 4ea1430 - the deadlock itself predates TASK-047, but TASK-047 is what exposed it on live pages: sweep #8's diag for getbootstrap was `TypeError: Object has no member 'addEventListener'`, i.e. the page's scripts died before they could register an observer; TASK-047 implemented `addEventListener`, the scripts now reach `new IntersectionObserver(...)`, and the latent deadlock fires. LOCATION, from a SIGQUIT goroutine dump of the merged build on getbootstrap (saved /tmp/t50-hang.err, 49 KB): goroutine 1 is `[sync.Mutex.Lock]` in `js.(*Runtime).jsGetShadowRoot` (internal/js/shadow_dom.go:119) called from `setupDOM.func56` (internal/js/js.go:846) through a goja property getter, called from goja `Object.Export`, called from `js.(*Runtime).CheckIntersections` (internal/js/intersection.go:257), from `engine.(*Session).Reflow` (internal/js/../engine/engine.go:994), from `engine.NewSession` (engine.go:285), from cmd/goosie/document_loader.go:394 - i.e. the load path, not the screenshot driver. The getters are enumerable by design (`internal/js/shadow_dom.go:21-32` and `internal/js/js.go:1422-1436` define `parentNode` and `shadowRoot` with `enumerable: true`), and `CheckIntersections` takes `r.mu` at intersection.go:254 before the `Export()` at :311, so the lock is taken twice on one stack. Blast radius: every page that observes an element is a hard hang with no timeout of its own - the process is idle (0.36 s CPU after 60 s, sockets CLOSED), so it is not a slow load. Bisect: binary built at a5c54245 renders getbootstrap in 1.2 s and vietnamnet in 2.3 s on this host today (rc 0 each, so the sites themselves are fine); binary built at 4ea1430 (TASK-047 merged, TASK-050 not) times out on both at 90 s. TASK-050 is exonerated. Why the sibling observers do not share the bug: MutationObserver (internal/js/mutation_observer.go:104) and ResizeObserver (internal/js/resize_observer.go:92) read `__nid__` at observe() time and keep a *dom.Node, so they never export a JS object under a lock. What closing needs: capture the node ID in `intersectionObserve`, store it on `IntersectionEntry`, and use it in `CheckIntersections` with no `Export()` and no goja property access while `r.mu` is held; an oracle that fails by watchdog timeout if the load deadlocks; and a re-run of the two live URLs plus the 100-site sweep. Fix: IntersectionEntry.targetID is captured from __nid__ inside intersectionObserve (default -1 for a non-node argument), and CheckIntersections resolves geometry through intersectionRectOf, which takes r.mu for one nodeRegistry map read and performs no goja property access or Export; the node is then translated to dom.Node.ID because elementRects is keyed by node ID while the old code looked it up with the wrapper ID - the two allocators differ, so old geometry only matched by coincidence. Mutation M01 (restore the Export()-under-r.mu loop) was re-run by the integrator: rc 1, TestIntersectionObserverCheckReturns, TestIntersectionObserverDoesNotFireForOffscreenTarget and TestNewSessionWithIntersectionObserverReturns each fail at exactly 10.00 s with the deadlock message; restore byte-identical, rc 0. Gates on merged main: go test -count=1 ./... rc 0 (43 ok), go vet -all rc 0, archtest rc 0, gofmt empty, go test -race ./internal/js ./test/js rc 0. Fixture js-dom/03-intersection-observer-first-reflow.html scores 97.56% PASS (IoU 0.984375, coverage 0.9966953658407048); corpus 93/93 average 96.23%, known gaps 5/10 unchanged, floor 92 -> 93; cases BR-234 (liveness/geometry) and BR-235 (integration + fixture). owner: internal/paint (builder_effects.go: paintBoxShadow and appendOuterBlurredField - every blurred outer layer as a separable Gaussian field delivered as per-pixel masked cells, clipped to the outside of the border box)
summary: Goosie's box-shadow blur is a small stack of hard layers rather than a Gaussian, so the ring and the falloff outside the box diverge from Chromium.
evidence:
Opened while reviewing TASK-053 (docs/tasks/TASK-053-ANON-BOX-PAINT-LAYERS.md §9.2 limit 3, §9.3 item 3) on 2026-10-26 and closed by BR-281 (docs/qa-test-catalog.md) on 2026-11-13. The three things this entry asked for are what shipped: a blur model measured against Chromium at several radii and offsets, a pixel oracle that sweeps the falloff instead of sampling one point, and a fixture that pins the profile.

The law, measured (Playwright deviceScaleFactor 1 + PIL, alpha = (240-R)/240 for pure blue over rgb(240,240,240), probes /tmp/sb3 and /tmp/sb5): sigma = blur/2; the pixel whose centre sits at p = coord+0.5 keeps Phi((hi-p)/sigma) - Phi((lo-p)/sigma) of the declared alpha on each axis, lo/hi being the shadow rect's edges (border box + offset + spread); the two axes multiply; ink is clipped to the outside of the border box; support is ceil(3*sigma) - measured as the last inked column at blur 2 (3px), 8 (12px), 16 (24px) and 40 (60px), every one 3.0 sigma - and blur 0 keeps the hard ring path it already had.

Three laws behind the falloff were being guessed at, each now measured with its own oracle. The parser rejected a negative spread, so `0 0 8px -4px` lost the whole declaration while Chromium paints it (the sweep's blur_8_spread_-4 row is Chromium's own ink). A shadow rect with no span painted ink at all: the 0x0, 40x0 and 0x40 boxes of /tmp/sb4/probe.html with `0 1px 4px rgba(0,128,255,.9)` read 0 ink pixels, so this is the second defect underneath the GOOSIE-LIVE-006 corner smudge, whose suppression half had already closed at BR-196. And the outer layer loop ran front-to-back, putting the last declared shadow on top; measured with two opaque hard rings, `0 0 0 10px red, 0 0 0 4px green` reads red across all 10px in Chromium and green across its 4px declared the other way round.

The fit is 2,261 pixels swept at blurs 1-40, spreads -4 to 10, offsets -20 to 10, alphas .25 to 1, a 12px band, a 10px strip, a translucent border and an opaque background: rms 0.0036, worst pixel 0.0132 - 3.2 levels of the 240-step ramp - so the oracle holds +-0.02 and a hard layer 0.004. The engine delivers the field as masked cells of at most 64px per side, tiled over four disjoint strips, sharing blurCoverage, fieldMaskCap and fieldMaskBudget with the inset path (BR-277) so one primitive answers for both edges.

This entry's own pixel stopped being an outlier: on the anonymous-band probe (330,60) moved from (213,59,59) to (250,232,232) against Chromium's (249,230,230), and the run-once document now changes 15,332 px against Chromium's 16,636 - the whole 1,304-px difference is one level deep at the edge of the support, recorded against GOOSIE-INSETTAIL-001 because it shares that defect's candidate cause and its sign (under-ink in the far tail).

What this entry does not close is registered with its own measurements: GOOSIE-SHADOWARC-001 and GOOSIE-SHADOWBUDGET-001, the two exception paths that still draw concentric rings.

All 116 other fixtures are digit-identical between those two runs (0 fixtures move by more than 0.0005: `07-shadows` 93.503, `21-inset-box-shadow` 98.367, `17-anonymous-block-shadow-once` 96.65 on both sides), so the change touches only documents carrying an inherited text-shadow. summary: `mask-image` paints against the whole box instead of honouring mask size/position/repeat, and gradient masks are not implemented at all.
evidence: GOOSIE-MASKPAINT-001 - measured while reviewing TASK-053 (docs/tasks/TASK-053-ANON-BOX-PAINT-LAYERS.md §9.1 and §9.2 limit 4), 2026-10-26. 400x200 probe, DPR 1, effect = |with declaration - without| on the same document: `mask-image: url(m.svg)` changes 22,773 px in Goosie (the whole 300x76 box) against Chromium's 110; Chromium's relative URL does not resolve on that probe, so the stronger comparison is the gradient row: `mask-image: linear-gradient(...)` changes 11,510 px plain and 11,519 with anonymous bands in Chromium, and 0/0 in Goosie because gradient masks are unimplemented. owner: unassigned (engine image table + reflow/paint; same area as TASK-052's script image loader)
summary: An image source a script assigns after document load is decoded but never attached to layout or paint: the element keeps its box, onload reports naturalWidth/naturalHeight, and the box paints empty. Only sources already present when NewSession collects images reach the paint-time table.
evidence: Measured by the integrator on merged main 2026-10-26 with a throwaway `package engine_test` probe (run once, then deleted). Page: `` plus one script, run through `engine.NewSession` (real js runtime, no stub). Assigning `i.src` to a `data:image/png` (7x9) inside the parse-time script: after NewSession the title reads `LOADED 7x9`, the arena box is 70x90, and the box object has `Image` attached (7x9) - it paints. Assigning the same source from `setTimeout(...,0)` and pumping the loop with `Session.PumpJS` until the title changes: title is again `LOADED 7x9` (so fetch/decode and the load event really happened) and the box is still 70x90, but the box object's `Image` is **nil** - there is nothing to draw. CODE PATH, read the same day: the paint-time table is `Session.images` (map[dom.NodeID]image.Image), filled only by `fetchImages` during `NewSession` (`internal/engine/engine.go:832`), and reflow attaches only entries from that map (`internal/engine/engine.go:956-958`). `Session.LoadScriptImage` (`internal/engine/script_image.go:55-97`) decodes the bytes, charges the reservation and reports `LoadedImage{Src, Width, Height}` to internal/js, but deliberately keeps no pixels and writes nothing to `Session.images` (its own comment says paint cannot reach it). After document load, nothing ever adds an entry, so a lazy source can never paint, in any mode. IMPACT: the common lazy-image patterns - `data-src`/`data-original` swaps, IntersectionObserver reveals, `loading=lazy` polyfills, ad slots that set `.src` from a timer - all render as empty boxes in Goosie while Chromium draws the image. This is a paint defect, not a script-interface defect; TASK-052's image oracles (BR-244..246, BR-248, BR-249) cover the interface and admission, and this id is what they do not cover. WHAT CLOSING NEEDS: retain the decoded pixels for a node that is in the document (and only then), key them in the paint-time table, update the intrinsic-size input the arena uses, and request a reflow/damage so the box repaints; keep the decoded-pixel reservation charged while the pixels are retained and release them on re-navigation/replacement, exactly as the parse-time path does. The oracle has to assert pixels (a non-nil box image / painted colour), not just naturalWidth - measured here, naturalWidth is already correct while the box is blank. Closed on 2026-10-26 by TASK-057 (merge c4463f2 onto 174a14a) and registration f1b89ab. Fix: LoadedImage.Pixels carries the decoded image opaquely across the js boundary; Options.ImagePixelSink is installed next to SetImageLoader and called in applyImageResult's success branch after the state update and before the load event, never on error; PumpJS drains recorded results after Tick/TickRAF, attaches only when the node is connected, is an , and its src attribute still equals the raw source that produced the pixels, reconciles retained entries (drop on disconnect or src change), and forces exactly one Reflow when RestyleAndReflow did not already build layout (WorkCounts().LayoutBuilds probe). A dropped entry does not refund its decoded-pixel reservation. Oracles BR-250..BR-252 plus TestDetachedScriptImageIsNeverRetained and TestScriptImageDropKeepsPixelReservation; all mutations behaved (M01 sink no-op and M02 no forced layout red on BR-250/251, M03 skip identity checks red on BR-252 and the detached test, M04 refund probe rejected by the reservation test). Re-measured on the combined tree with the real binary after TASK-056's paced pump landed: the after-load page paints 6,300 blue pixels at -dpr 1, identical to the during-parse control. go test ./... rc 0 (43 packages); race, vet, archtest and gofmt clean. Out of scope and not measured: srcset/, CSS backgrounds, canvas drawImage, and the stale parse-time case (TASK-057 section 3.4).

owner: unassigned (cmd/goosie paced runs: pump wiring and image fetch context)
summary: Paced headless runs (-screenshot, -gate, -bench) never pump the page's JS event loop, and they cancel in-flight script-image fetches when the load call returns. Timers, RAF callbacks and async load completions therefore never run, so screenshots cannot represent any page whose final paint depends on post-load script - while the Chromium side of the same comparison has run them.
evidence: Measured by the integrator on merged main 2026-10-26 against a local HTTP server. (1) NO PUMP: a page that sets `document.body.style.background` from `setTimeout(...,0)` keeps the pre-timer colour after `-gate -frames 200` (3.49 s at 57 fps). The tick that drives JS exists only on the interactive chrome window: `cmd/goosie/main.go:528-529` calls `cw.setTick(..., f.pumpChrome)` inside `if cw, ok := f.window.(*chromeWindow)`, and a paced run builds no toolbar/tab manager, so `f.window` is not a chromeWindow and nothing calls `Session.PumpJS` (`cmd/goosie/presentation.go:35-50`, reached only from `pumpChrome` in `cmd/goosie/media.go:37-39`). Microtasks queued by an image loader therefore stay queued, and `complete` stays false forever - a state no browser is in seconds after load. (2) CANCELED FETCH: a page doing `var i=new Image(); i.src='http://127.0.0.1:PORT/x.png'` calls the loader (`DBG` instrumentation on a temporary build, restored byte-identical) and the goroutine enters `fetchImageBytes`, but the client reports `context canceled`; the local server never logs `GET /x.png` in either `-screenshot` or the 200-frame gate run. Cause: `cmd/goosie/document_loader.go:290-296` creates the image context with `context.WithTimeout` and `defer imgCancel()`, which fires when `loadURLCtx` returns. Parsed `` fetches finish inside that call (a control page with a parsed `` did log the request and painted 70x90 = 6300 px blue), so the cancel only hits work that outlives the call - exactly the script-image path. (3) CONTROL, same page, when pumped: an engine session probe (`PumpJS` loop) logs `LOADED 7x9` and a `cmd/goosie` `loadURLCtx` probe (temporary `package main` test, deleted) fetched `/x.png` and reported `LOADED 7x9`; so the machinery works when the loop runs and the context lives. The failure is in the paced run's wiring, not in the image loader or the DOM binding. IMPACT: the live sweep's BLANK_OUTPUT / LAYOUT_EMPTY / MISSING_REGIONS labels cannot distinguish 'engine cannot paint' from 'paced run never let the page's script finish'; the Chromium capture can. Attribution of any sweep row whose page reveals content from a timer, RAF or a script-assigned source must say so instead of blaming layout. WHAT CLOSING NEEDS: give paced runs a pump (call `Session.PumpJS` once per frame for the active session, as the interactive chrome tick does) and keep script-image fetches alive for the session's lifetime rather than the load call - the engine's own ImageFetchBudget (6 s) already bounds them. Then re-measure the same two pages: the timer colour and the `/x.png` server hit must both appear before the screenshot is written. Closed on 2026-10-26 by TASK-056 (commit 174a14a) and registration f1b89ab. Fix: driver and steadyDriver run one watchVsync hook on every surface.EvVsync, on the pump goroutine and before ready is consulted; f.pumpJS dispatches to pumpPaced/repaintPaced when there is no tab manager, and repaintPaced republishes the plan when Session.BackgroundColor changes; the interactive darwin path is unchanged. loadURLCtx no longer defers imgCancel for the script-image case; the lifetime is ImageFetchBudget (6 s, unchanged) plus the navigation context. Oracles BR-253..BR-255 through the real -screenshot binary plus a gate probe: M01 (no hook) red on all four, M02 (restore defer imgCancel) red on BR-254 with 'context canceled' after the 50 ms hold, M03 (a second pump goroutine) produced 4 data-race reports and rc 66 under go build -race, which is the measured single-goroutine requirement. Built-binary re-measurement: the timer colour #ff0000 appears; the local server logs GET /x.png with the request context alive after the hold in both -screenshot and -gate -frames 200; the gate run also logs the timer's GET /ping. go test ./... rc 0 (43 packages); race, vet, archtest and gofmt clean. Not measured: the native interactive path, -bench rate, and an in-process assertion of the exact onload instant (BR-254 orders it server-side).

summary: A live sweep names only the commit its binary's tree pointed at, so a binary built from a dirty working tree is scored as that commit and in-progress edits are attributed to a released SHA.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-010, measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while attributing sweep 11. The report docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-26T0606Z-bdd545f3.md said 'source 80a2f617, binary bin/goosie, SHA-256 a41f516a...', but `go version -m bin/goosie` records `build vcs.modified=true` and the module line ends `...+dirty`: the make-built binary contained the working tree, not commit 80a2f617. Proof by rebuild: a clean checkout of 80a2f617 built on this host gives SHA-256 0393844b4b83535711eeaf5461cba57ccf66d0d38ea5fb6af961eda035f7ed4c, a different artifact. The dirty files observed in the tree at the time included internal/dom/events.go, internal/js/js.go and internal/layout/block.go; two of them were restored by their author before they could be captured, so the exact content the sweep compiled is unrecoverable and that run is not attributable to any commit. The harness could not have noticed: capture_build() recorded the source SHA, binary path and binary hash for GOOSIE-LIVE-008 but never read Go's VCS stamp, and only `vcs.modified` distinguishes HEAD-as-pointer from HEAD-as-built. Sweep 11's report was parked at /tmp/sweep11-dirty/ and deliberately not committed; it is evidence for this entry, not a measurement of main. summary: fetch ignores RequestInit.signal, so AbortController.abort() cannot cancel an in-flight request: the promise still resolves with the late response and its body is delivered to the page.
evidence: Found while closing BR-119/BR-120 on 2026-11-02. AbortController itself exists (internal/js/abort_controller.go) and test/js/abort_controller_test.go pins its signal, reason, and onabort behaviour, but the fetch path never reads the signal: parseFetchOpts (internal/js/fetch.go:143-184) copies only method, body, credentials, and headers, and runFetch settles on the client result with no abort check. Measured directly with a temporary probe against a gate-blocked HTTPFetcher: fetch('/slow', {signal: controller.signal}) was started, controller.abort() ran while the request was still blocked, the gate was then released, and the script observed lateBody="late" with rejected=false - the late response was applied instead of aborting. Consequence: a page that aborts a slow request keeps consuming its response and runs its then handler. Closing needs FetchOptions to carry the AbortSignal, fetch to reject with an AbortError when the signal is already or becomes aborted, the late response/body not to be applied, and an end-to-end oracle in test/js before BR-123 can be marked PASS. CLOSED 2026-11-05 after re-measuring the whole abort contract against Chromium 153 (scripts/verify-br123-fetch-abort.js, 27 checks, exit 0): fetch reads RequestInit.signal (internal/js/fetch.go:followFetchSignal), a mid-flight abort rejects at once, a pre-aborted signal never reaches the client (measured server-side: preAbortedSlowHits: 0), and the late response is dropped - logLater stays ["catch:AbortError"] with no `then`. The claim that the signal is ignored had been stale since the fetchAbort slice that closed BR-123 on 2026-11-02; this slice found and fixed what the measurement *did* show: the rejection was a plain string, so err.name/err instanceof DOMException were undefined/false and every custom reason was stringified. Goosie now rejects with signal.reason by identity - a default abort is the DOMException {ctor:"DOMException", name:"AbortError", message:"signal is aborted without reason", code:20}, abort({code:7}) arrives as the same object (identity:true), abort(new Error('boom')) stays an Error, abort(0) stays a number and abort(null) stays null - and a `signal` that is not an AbortSignal rejects with the TypeError carrying Chromium's exact message without issuing a request (test/js/fetch_abort_reason_test.go, seven oracles, mutation-proven MU1-MU5). Residuals found by the same measurement are recorded as GOOSIE-FETCH-CANCEL-001, GOOSIE-SIGNALTIMEOUT-001 and GOOSIE-DOMEXCSHAPE-001.

owner: internal/paint (builder_effects.go: paintInsetBoxShadow and appendInsetBlurredField - every inset layer as a measured Gaussian field delivered as per-pixel masked cells)
summary: An `inset` box-shadow layer paints nothing: the builder skips every inset layer, so a card that carries its depth as an inner shadow loses that layer while Chromium keeps it.
evidence:
Disclosed while writing the BR-073 effects oracles on 2026-11-04 and closed by BR-277 (docs/qa-test-catalog.md) on 2026-11-13. The three things this entry asked for are what shipped: an interior clip, a Chromium-measured falloff profile, and an oracle that sweeps the inset band instead of asserting its absence.

Measured laws (Playwright deviceScaleFactor 1 + PIL, alpha = (240-R)/240 for pure blue over rgb(240,240,240), 200x100 boxes, probes /tmp/is/probe6.html and probe8.html): sharp depth per side = spread + the offset component aimed at that edge, signed (left spread+dx, right spread-dx, top spread+dy, bottom spread-dy); sigma = blur/2; coverage x device pixels in from an edge = Phi((depth-x)/sigma); the field is separable, total = 1-(1-cx)(1-cy) with cx the sum of the two edges' coverages clamped to 1; ink is clipped to the padding box and paints over the background and under the border (CSS Backgrounds 4.4), measured through `border:4px rgba(255,0,0,.5)`: the border band reads (248,120,120), so the blue stops at the padding edge, and its peak is still 0.221 as on a borderless box; reach = ceil(clamp(depth+2*sigma, <= dim)).

Why the mask path and not four ramps: source-over multiplies the un-inked fraction, so stacked edge ramps put 0.521 at a translucent corner where Chromium reads 0.367 - an a(1-a)cx*cy error. The builder now emits four edge ramps trimmed short of the corners plus one masked CmdFill per corner (eight cells, verified to overlap nowhere and to leave the padding box nowhere), and where two bands cross there is no corner left to cut, so the cells tile the whole padding box on a 64px grid (insetMaskCap) up to insetMaskBudget = 65536 px.

Red by mutation on the fixed tree, three claims measured separately: insetMaskBudget = 0 -> `inset 4px 0 8px 2px rgba(0,0,255,0.5)` col-mid (6,0) reads 0.479 where Chromium measured 0.400 (+0.079), (6,1) +0.067, (6,2) +0.042, and the structural oracle fails because the crossing box emits 4 ramps and 0 cells instead of 1 cell; deleting the four corner-cell calls -> 25 red assertions across 3 tests, with the corner squares at 0.000 where Chromium reads 0.338, 0.467 and 0.708 on the diagonal (the pixels no ramp can reach); dropping the far-edge term from insetFieldCoverage -> 23 red, all in the crossing-band sweep, the far side of a 12px row at 0.000 against Chromium's 0.221. Every other test stayed green under each mutation. Against HEAD's own engine (git worktree at 8f41f301, grep -c paintInsetBoxShadow = 0) the same oracle is 7 tests and 190 assertions red with every gap 0.000 - max 0.500.

Pixel evidence: testdata/render/css-features/21-inset-box-shadow.html scored twice on one corpus - 98.37% PASS on the fixed tree (worst_region_iou=1.0, coverage_ratio=0.9997, 0 blank bands) against 87.37% FAIL on the HEAD binary (iou=0.9916, coverage=0.9806, 0 blank bands); corpus 116/116 (100.0%) average 96.49% exit 0 after, 115/116 average 96.39% exit 1 before; css-features/07-shadows.png moved 93.26 -> 93.50% toward Chromium and css-features/17-anonymous-block-shadow-once.png held 96.65% to the digit. owner: closed by the GOOSIE-LISTBOX-001 viewport-placement and row-window slice, 2026-11-04
summary: A <select> listbox popup always opens below the control and never scrolls: a select near the bottom of the viewport pushes rows off-screen, and an option list taller than the panel shows only the first rows.
evidence: Disclosed while implementing the BR-101 mouse half on 2026-11-04. internal/engine/listbox.go:listBoxLocked places the panel at box.Y1 unconditionally - there is no viewport-height test and no flip above the control - and the row list is the whole option list with no scroll offset or clamp, so rows past the viewport bottom are painted and hit-tested outside what a user can see. test/paint/select_popup_test.go:TestOpenListboxPaintsOneRowPerOptionInOrder and test/engine/select_popup_test.go:TestListboxRowsAreInsetUniformAndStacked pin the panel below the control as CURRENT behaviour, so a flip fix must retake those assertions rather than fail the gate. No measured reference exists for the target: Chromium's closed-select popup is OS-native and invisible to page script, which is exactly why scripts/verify-br101-select-popup.js anchors on the in-page listbox (size=3) for row geometry and on page.mouse.click for the observable DOM outcome. Closing needs a viewport-placement rule measured against a real browser (flip up when the panel would overflow, clamp to the viewport when it still does not fit) plus a scroll offset for lists longer than the panel, with the pointer and the paint path reading the same rows so the single-owner rule in listBoxLocked holds. BR-101 itself is signed off PASS because its acceptance condition is that value, focus and paint match the choice, which holds for every row the panel shows. Closed by the GOOSIE-LISTBOX-001 viewport-placement and row-window slice, 2026-11-04. internal/engine/listbox.go:listBoxLocked now owns one placement rule for both paint and the pointer: the panel may only cover the viewport the user is looking at, it opens above the control when the whole list does not fit below and more room is above, and a list longer than either side shows a window of whole rows whose first option is max(0, selectedIndex-visible+1) - exactly the topRow the anchor's ROW-WINDOW lines measure on Chromium's in-page listbox. evidence: Closed 2026-11-06 by the BR-101 row-height slice, on Chromium 153.0.8010.12, measured by the new anchor scripts/verify-br101-listbox-rowheight.js, which renders eleven in-page listboxes (<select size=3>, the form the popup's rows are anchored on since the native popup is invisible to page script, GOOSIE-LISTBOX-002) and reads every option's getBoundingClientRect plus computed style.
