owner: internal/style/gradient.go stopPosition/parseGradientStops/StopsAlong + internal/paint/builder_style.go gradientLineLength/radialRadius (closed: lengths ride the stop through the cascade and resolve at paint)
summary: A gradient stop position written as a <length> now rides the stop (Px, PxSet) through the cascade - which cannot turn a length into a fraction of a line it cannot measure - and resolves at paint time against the gradient line of the command rect, the same measure the rasterizer re-derives per pixel. Ramps with px stops paint at the authored offsets instead of vanishing or spreading evenly. Chromium parity holds for px spellings; non-px length units stay open as a disclosed residual.
evidence: Closed 2026-11-06 by the BR-074 gradient length-stop slice, on Chromium 1.63 measured by scripts/verify-br074-color-idle-scroll.js (three runs identical). The anchor's SYNTAX page gained a second column (SYNTAX_B) for the two spellings whose Goosie answer needs more than the written positions: px-anchor-dist `linear-gradient(180deg,#f00 45px,#0f0,#00f)` answers rgb(255,0,0) rgb(255,0,0) rgb(238,17,0) at 25/50/75% - solid red through 50% proves the unpositioned tail anchors at the END of the laid-out line (middle stop at 52.5px, halfway from the 45px anchor), where even distribution over the stops would answer (0,255,0); and pct-px-mixed `linear-gradient(180deg,#f00 25%,#0f0 30px,#00b)` answers rgb(247,9,0) rgb(0,250,3) rgb(0,123,97), so the % stop converts onto the SAME measured line the px length resolves against. Goosie's fix: stopPosition claims `Npx` tokens as stopPos{px,isPx} (other units keep the old fall-through), parseGradientStops emits px stops as {At:-1, Px, PxSet} and orders double positions only within one kind, distributeStops returns untouched any ramp carrying a length stop, and paint resolves per tile: builder_style.go gradientLineLength computes |W.sin| + |H.cos| of the command rect - the tile clipped to the clip box, exactly the rect internal/frame.FillLinearGradient divides distance by - radialGradient mirrors FillRadialGradient's radius, and style.StopsAlong converts px to fractions, % stops via At x lineLen onto that line, distributes the unpositioned rest through the shared fillPositions core (one algorithm for cascade fractions and paint pixels; the monotonic clamp keeps backwards runs in order). Pure-fraction ramps are byte-identical: every pre-existing cascade test passes verbatim. Oracles: test/style/gradient_px_test.go (two tests, // qc:BR-074) pin that px stops ride unresolved (At -1, Px carried) and that a mixed %/px/unpositioned ramp defers distribution; test/paint/color_idle_scroll_test.go:TestGradientStopsWithUnitlessZeroPositionsPaint grew from 6 to 12 wants over fixture boxes #pxa/#pxm/#pxd/#pxc, pinning the four measured spellings at 25/50/75% (tolerance 0-3: Chromium's dither amplitude scales with the ramp slope - 255 units over 30px here against 170 over 1600 on the tall box). The style oracles were watched red on the pre-fix tree (stops = 0 for px-ends; the mixed ramp answered [0 0.5 1]); the paint wants' red state is evidenced by mutant M1, which reproduces the pre-fix parse exactly and reddens all twelve. Correcting the old record's diagnosis: px-mid did NOT reach distributeStops with kept colours - on the pre-fix tree BOTH px spellings dropped the whole ramp at ParseColor, and the [0 0.5 1] answer came from an accident: css.parseHex reads `#a00 30px` after stripping `#` as an eight-character garbage hex (len('a00 30px')==8 hits case 8) while `#0a0 0px` (seven chars) fails - so one spelling lost the background and the other lost the geometry through the same fall-through. owner: closed: internal/style/gradient.go parseRadialGradientArgs (token-grammar header) + internal/paint/builder_style.go radialRadii (the CSS sizing table resolves once at paint; the command carries Rx/Ry)
summary: A radial-gradient's ending shape is now sized by its declaration: the header parser reads shape, size keyword and `at` position (before this slice only bare `circle`/`ellipse` survived the parse - every other header form dropped the whole gradient), paint resolves the CSS sizing table against the command rect and carries concrete per-axis radii on the command, and the rasterizer blends across them. A circle reaches the farthest corner, the size keywords pick their sides and corners, an ellipse stretches per axis, and the painted ramp matches Chromium at every measured probe. Residuals disclosed: the explicit two-length radii form, non-px position/stop units, degenerate edge centres, and the unmeasured ellipse closest-corner cell.
evidence: Closed 2026-11-06 by the radial ending-shape slice, on Chromium 1.63 measured by scripts/verify-radialgrad-geometry.js (9 pixel boxes, 9 syntax cells; anchor rerun clean). Correcting the old record's diagnosis FIRST: the Size keyword did not merely fail to reach the rasterizer - the parse dropped it. The old parser matched whole space-separated parts against a token switch, so of every header form Chromium keeps (SYNTAX page: circle and ellipse with each size keyword, `at` positions, explicit radii; all kept=YES with computed serializations recorded in the script), only bare `circle`/`ellipse` parsed: `circle closest-side at 25% 25%`, `ellipse closest-side`, bare `closest-side` and `circle at 30px 30px` all fell through to the stop parser and dropped the WHOLE gradient, which is why five of the anchor's boxes painted nothing at all pre-fix (white at every probe). Goosie's fix has two halves. evidence: Closed by the OPTIONAX role slice, 2026-11-05, on Chromium 153.0.8010.12, measured by the new anchor scripts/verify-optionax-roles.js (182 checks, 0 failed, exit 0), which walks the CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree childId graph over seventeen widget shapes and compares role, name, value, the FULL property set and every option node's properties. The shape that falsifies the obvious rule is <select multiple size="1"> -> {"role":"combobox","value":"Mm One"} with the closed box's full property set, so `multiple` alone decides nothing; it only raises the used-size default to 4, which is why multiple+size="0" is a listbox. The IDL getter cannot be read either: measured select.size = 0 for an absent attribute on both a single and a multiple control. Goosie's owner is now dom.SelectAnnouncesListbox (internal/dom/node.go:605, selectDisplaySize > 1 - the same used-size function the paint shape already reads), and internal/engine/accessibility.go takes BOTH the role and the announced display string from that one decision, replacing the old dom.SelectIsPopupStyle gate. An authored role="listbox" now resolves to the same role (the anchor's aria-listbox case answers {"role":"listbox","name":"Authored listbox"} with its option as a child and NO activedescendant of its own), which the ARIA token map used to fold into a group. Seven mutants of the fixed tree each reddened an oracle and were restored: (M1) let `multiple` decide the role -> `:63: <select id="s" multiple size="1">... announces "listbox", want "combobox"` and `:99: multiple size=1 role = "listbox", want combobox`; (M2) gate the display on the paint shape instead of the role -> `:102: multiple size=1 value = "", want the display string "Mm One"`; (M5) emit combobox always -> the five-listbox-shape list above; (M6) drop the ARIA token case -> `:179: authored listbox role = "group", want listbox`; (M7) read the used size as >= 1 -> `accessibility_option_label_test.go:66: no combo box in the accessibility tree` and three more, because every closed select became a list; (M8) mislabel the new role's String() -> `ax_role_test.go:29: RoleListBox String() = "group", want the ARIA token listbox`. summary: A closed combobox hangs its options under a non-ignored MenuListPopup node while a listbox hangs them under an ignored `none` wrapper, so one child list cannot serve both shapes; Goosie emits options directly under the control. The container's AppKit role string, the activedescendant host move that comes with it, the authored-widget property sets and the darwin transport of ax.Node.Props are all measured-but-unemitted or unmeasurable without a display host.
evidence: Opened 2026-11-06 by the OPTIONAX property slice, which closed the measurable half of GOOSIE-OPTIONAX-004 and split this off rather than guess it. Every measurement below is printed and pinned by scripts/verify-optionax-props.js (Chromium 153.0.8010.12, 46 fixtures, 324 checks, 0 failed). (1) STRUCTURE: a closed combobox has exactly one non-ignored child with role MenuListPopup, name "", no value and props {} when unfocused (its activedescendant when the control is focused); it exists even when the select has ZERO options, and it is the parent of both the option nodes and the optgroup `group` nodes. A listbox has no such node - the same children hang under an ignored `none` wrapper that a tree walk must splice through. Emitting the container in Goosie invalidates 47 .Children assertions across five files (test/engine/option_ax_roles_test.go, option_value_test.go, accessibility_test.go, accessibility_option_label_test.go, option_ax_surfaces_test.go), which is why it is a slice of its own and not a rider. (2) APPKIT: the container needs a role code, and the right AppKit role string is NOT measurable in a headless session - no assistive client runs here, and axRoleCode in internal/platform/darwin/window.go would silently fall through to `default: GOOSIE_AX_GROUP` for any new code, so a wrong choice passes every test this repo can run. The same gap already covers the two select roles (GOOSIE_AX_COMBO_BOX -> NSAccessibilityPopUpButtonRole, GOOSIE_AX_LIST_BOX -> NSAccessibilityListRole, written in the existing table's style and confirmed by no client). (3) ACTIVEDESCENDANT HOST: the measured host is the control for an open listbox but the MenuListPopup child for a closed combobox, so moving the container also moves the property; Goosie currently answers it on the control for both. (4) ax.Node.Selected IS NOT PRUNED while the `selected` property is: Chromium's disabled option answers {disabled:true} alone, and the platform shims read the Selected field, so a darwin client still hears the selection on a disabled option. Whether the field should follow the property or keep reporting DOM selectedness needs the client to compare against. (5) AUTHORED WIDGETS: measured but not emitted - div[role=listbox] answers {multiselectable:false, orientation:"vertical", required:false} with its role=option child answering {selected:false}, and div[role=combobox][aria-haspopup=listbox][aria-expanded=false][tabindex=0] answers {expanded:false, focusable:true, hasPopup:"listbox", required:false}. Goosie resolves the ARIA role token but attaches no properties to a non-select widget. (6) TRANSPORT: GoosieAxNode (internal/platform/darwin/shim.h:232-282) has role, geometry, identifier/label/value/href, flags and child links but NO property field, so Node.Props stops at the Go side of the shim; macOS behaviour is unchanged by this slice, which is also why nothing had to be guessed. (7) expanded:true: a native popup's expanded state is not observable from a headless host, so the open half of the expanded property stays unmeasured. Closing needs a display host plus VoiceOver (or an equivalent assistive client) to compare AppKit role strings and attribute values against; until then this record is the honest residual and no rule here should be encoded from memory.

summary: A line box whose content is only atomic inline-level boxes pays nothing for the containing block's font: the strut's descent below the baseline is missing, so every such row is short and each block below it drifts up by a multiple of that error.
evidence:
Opened 2026-11-12 by a fixture, not by a plan, while closing GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001. Measured on the same markup on both engines: a `
` holding two `display:inline-block` boxes of `height:24px` with `1px` borders and `margin-bottom:10px`, body `16px sans-serif`, `line-height: normal`, viewport 800x600, no text node on the line. Chromium puts the rows at y=20 and y=60 and measures 40px for each: 26 border-box + 10 margin + 4 of descent below the baseline. Goosie puts them at y=20 and y=56 and measures 36 - exactly the tallest atomic's margin-border box. The reference `

` after the two rows lands at y=116 in Chromium and y=108 in Goosie, so the error is per row and compounds down the page (the first version of testdata/render/css-features/19-attr-selector-escaped-value.html stacked eight such rows, lost 32px, and scored 84.59% FAIL with a blank band at y=346-369 while the selector fix itself was pixel-correct). CSS 2.1 10.6.1 requires a line box to be at least as tall as the strut built from the block's own font metrics even when every inline-level box on the line is atomic, so the missing 4px is that descent. Mechanism read from the code, not guessed: `atomicInline` (internal/layout/inline.go:882,892) and `atomicInlineReplaced` (internal/layout/inline.go:928,933) contribute `lineH = k.BorderH() + k.MarginTop + k.MarginBottom` to `current.h`, and `runHeights` (internal/layout/inline.go:938) - the only place ascent, descent and half-leading are computed - is reached solely by text runs, so a line with no text run never sees the strut. The fixture now sets `vertical-align: top` on those boxes, which puts both engines at 36px per row and keeps its colour evidence attributable to the selector; that is a workaround for one page, not a fix, and every page whose lines hold only inline-blocks (icon strips, sprite rows, chip lists) keeps shifting. What closing needs: fold the containing block's strut into the line box when the line's content is only atomic inline-level boxes, one layout oracle pinning row height 40 and the following block's y=116 on exactly the markup measured here (Chromium numbers, measured 2026-11-12 with Playwright), a render fixture whose tail bands sit below several such rows so a short strut moves visible pixels, and Chromium measurements for the shapes that decide the rule rather than this one case: atomic plus text on one line, `vertical-align: top|middle|bottom` resolving over a strut, and an empty line in a block with a large font. CLOSED by d38a9669 (2026-11-12, BR-270). The rule resolves each side of the baseline on its own rather than by the scalar strut clamp it had: `atomicLineExtent(strutAbove, strutBelow, boxes)` returns `base = max(strutAbove, extent_i - below_i)` and `height = base + max(strutBelow, below_i)`, after which `top`/`bottom` boxes only stretch the height. `below_i` is what decides the shape and every value in it is measured on Chromium 2026-11-12, not recalled from 10.8: an empty or replaced box puts its bottom margin edge on the baseline (`below_i = 0`), so a 36px chip row gives 40 and a 20px image gives 24, while an inline-block with in-flow line boxes - and every form control, whose text lives in a shadow tree no arena walk can see, which is what `isFormControl` exists for - brings that line's own descent plus its padding, border and margin, so a 28px text chip beside a 36px empty one gives a 45px line with the text chip dropped 17px, and a lone control's line is exactly the control's own box (measured before this: a 26px input treated as replaced gained a second descent and the forms fixtures moved). BOTH line-building paths were short of the strut: `inlineInto`, and block.go's row path, which is what a container whose kids are all inline-blocks reaches instead of the inline pass (`flowsInlineContent == false`); `rowH` was deleted rather than left as a second source for the same number. summary: Controls that render a value get their box height from the document font instead of Chromium's 13.3333px UA control font, so they come out 3px short or more: a text field is 18 where the reference is 21, a select 18 against 19, a colour swatch 32x18 against 50x27.
evidence: Opened 2026-11-12 by the BR-274 slice, which fixed the *baseline* of the appearance-only widgets and had to state what it did not touch. The baseline of a value control comes from a text line inside the control, so its box height is that line's height - and Goosie builds it from the inherited document face while Chromium lays controls in its own UA font. Measured on Chromium (Playwright 2026-11-12, viewport 800x600, standards mode, `body { font: 16px sans-serif }`): `getComputedStyle` answers `font-size: 13.3333px` on text, number, select, button and textarea, and those boxes are 154x21 (text/number), 19 tall for select, `input[type=colour]` 50x27, `button` min-width 80x21. Goosie on the same markup answers 154x**18**, select 18, colour 32x**18** - one line of the 16px face (14/4/18), i.e. the document font, which is also why the swatch is 32 wide: the intrinsic sizes are constants in internal/layout/block.go:1784 rather than a derivation from a control font. BR-274's oracle rows f5/f6/f7 pin **Goosie's own** 18/21/18 answers instead of Chromium's, deliberately: the offsets are the part that was wrong and the heights are a separate defect, so a future change to control sizing must pass through this entry rather than slip past a baseline test - but every row under a control then inherits ~3px of vertical error per field, which is what keeps `forms/01-text-inputs` and `forms/04-advanced-inputs` below the corpus average. Second, smaller gap in the same classifier, measured on both binaries so it is not attributable to BR-274: `input[type=image]` is a replaced box - neither an appearance widget nor a control with a text line - but `boxOfAtomic` routes it to the interior branch, so a 13x13 image input answers **20/4** under host metrics where Chromium answers **18/1**, the reference putting its baseline on the bottom margin edge like any other image. That row is absent from the unit oracle because the test harness has no image decoder (it returns line 0 and a negative offset there), so the pair above is dump-layout evidence against a reference probe, not a green assertion. What closing needs: a UA control font carried in the cascade (a computed 13.3333px on the shadow line, not a magic height in layout), the intrinsic-size table re-derived from that font so a field's box is one line of it, `input[type=image]` classified with images, and both re-scored through `make parity` on `forms/01`, `02`, `04`, `05`, `06`, `08` plus `html-features/01-forms-complete` rather than only by unit oracles. CLOSED by BR-276 (2026-11-13). The UA sheet now carries the control font - `input, select, button { font: 400 13.3333px Arial; font-style: normal }` in internal/style/style.go `uaCSS`, the same size in monospace for textarea and the date family - plus the chrome each control measured with getComputedStyle (text-like `box-sizing: content-box; border: 2px inset rgb(118,118,118); padding: 1px 2px`, the border-box list, the chromeless transparent list, button `#efefef` with `1px 6px` padding and a `2px outset` border, colour `1px solid` with `1px 2px`, the textarea and select rules), and `replacedSize` returns the CONTENT box that chrome leaves instead of the constants named above: text-like 145x15 -> border box **153x21** (Chromium 153x21), checkbox/radio 13x13, range 129x16, colour 44x23 -> **50x27**, time 72x20 -> **77x24**, date/month/week/datetime-local 119.328125x17.328125 / 149.328125x17.328125 / 141.328125x17.328125 / 179.328125x17.328125 -> the measured **124.328125 / 154.328125 / 146.328125 / 184.328125** x **21.328125**, file 253 x lh+6 -> **253x21**, and submit/reset/button sized by `estimateTextWidth` of their label with the 80px floor deleted because the reference measures `button "Go"` at 33.796875x21. `input[type=image]` left the control branch: inline.go's `isFormControl` excludes it and block.go routes it to the same `imgContentSize` as ``, so its baseline is the bottom margin edge - measured on both engines 13x13 border box, row **18**, top **1**, and identical to the `` beside it, which is the 20/4-vs-18/1 pair this entry named, now a green assertion rather than dump-layout evidence. Evidence: `test/layout/control_ua_box_test.go` (3 tests, 29 rows, `// qc:BR-276`) pins computed font/box-sizing/border widths+styles+colours/padding/background/display plus the border box plus the row height for every row, built on the six Chromium-measured faces BR-274 installed (plain `session()` metrics cannot reproduce a UA-font line height at all). Mutation on a worktree at 4198917d carrying only this slice's test files: **121 red assertions across 7 tests**, with BR-274's widget-baseline oracle and `TestReplacedInputTypesAreInlineLevel` still green, so the red is attributable here. Pixels: new fixture `testdata/render/forms/10-control-ua-boxes.html` **96.29% PASS** on the post binary and **86.29% FAIL** on the pre one; corpus **115/115 (100.0%)** average **96.47%** after, **114/115 exit 1** average **96.35%** before; `MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES` 114 -> 115. Two fixtures left `testdata/render-known-gaps.json` in the same commit (`forms/04-advanced-inputs`, `html-features/01-forms-complete`) because their controls now carry boxes and both measure 0 blank bands: the declarations were removed and the threshold was not touched. Author origin over UA measured, not assumed - the `.page` row (author `padding: 8px; border: 1px solid #ccc`) is **163x33 / row 33** in both engines. What this slice did NOT close, registered instead from the same measurement pass: GOOSIE-CONTROLWIDTH-001 (default widths need a per-character measure, and advances at the fractional 13.3333px come out ~2.5% short), GOOSIE-CONTROLINTERIOR-001 (file, the date family, colour, select and range paint a frame here where the reference paints the control's innards), GOOSIE-BEVELPAINT-001 (inset/outset are drawn as a flat strip), GOOSIE-IMAGEINPUT-001 (the image input's src is never fetched, so only width/height attributes reach the box), GOOSIE-FONTSHORTHANDWIDE-001 (a CSS-wide keyword in the `font` shorthand is dropped, which the new UA rule makes visible), and the file row's line height stays under GOOSIE-INLINEBASELINE-001 (22 here against Chromium's 21, because a chromeless control leaves the parent strut's descent as the only thing below its baseline). Roadmap: docs/roadmap-v2.md BR-276.

summary: `vertical-align: middle` resolves to the line's bottom edge because the value needs the parent font's x-height and no metric of this engine reports one: the box lands 6.19px low on a strut-height line and 22.19px low on a tall one.
evidence: Opened 2026-11-12 by the BR-272 slice, which resolved every other value of the property and left this one named in code: `atomicAlign` returns `atomicToMiddle`, `(lineFrame).atomicTop` has no case for it, so it falls through to the `bottom` branch. Measured on Chromium 2026-11-12 for a 4px inline-block chip: the reference offset is exactly `base - x-height/2 - extent/2` - 7.81 on the 16px strut line (base 14, x-height/2 4.19, extent/2 2) and 23.8125 on a `line-height: 50px` line (base 30) - and the x-height is a fact of the face, read directly with canvas `measureText('x').actualBoundingBoxAscent` at 16px sans-serif: 8.3671875 (0.523em). `cmd/dump-layout` answers 14 and 46 on those two lines, so the error is half a line on the strut and nearly a whole half of a 50px line on the tall one - visible wherever icons or inline-blocks are centred. The interface has nowhere to ask: `Metrics` (internal/frame) offers glyph advances and `LineMetrics(sizePx, slot) -> (ascent, descent, normalHeight)` only. What closing needs: x-height in that interface, the host face's value in internal/raster/fonts.go, a number for the fake `Metrics` the layout oracles already inject (so the oracle stays arithmetic rather than host-dependent), and the `atomicToMiddle` case in atomicTop. Distinct from `middle` on a run of glyphs, which is the same property's second gap (GOOSIE-VALIGNTEXT-001). ADDENDUM 2026-11-12, measured while BR-273 (e934dbbc) closed the rest of vertical-align: the same missing quantity now blocks the value on a *run of text* too. For a 16px run with `line-height:40px` on a 50px strut the reference answers content top **16.8125**, and the two stand-ins were both measured rather than assumed: the run's baseline position answers **16** (error 0.8125) and the line's bottom edge - what the atomic `middle` still falls back to - answers **21** (error 4.1875). BR-273 therefore routes a text run's `middle` to the baseline and leaves the atomic fallback alone, so the x-height fixes two paths at once and the gap does not depend on the run's own line height (it is half the x-height minus half the descent). Related: `sub` on a text run is exactly half this same x-height (measured 4.1875 against 8.375), so it closes here too - see GOOSIE-VALIGNSUB-001. ADDENDUM 2026-11-13, CLOSED by BR-275 (456f10d5). The metric exists: `Metrics.XHeightFixed(sizePx, slot)` (internal/layout/arena.go) returns the face's x-height in 26.6 fixed and `(Fonts).XHeightFixed` (internal/raster/fonts.go) reads `Metrics().XHeight` from golang.org/x/image/font, which already carries it, so no backend was added; the two `Metrics` fakes the line-box oracles install (`controlLineMetrics`, `chromiumLineMetrics`) answer 0.5234375em so those oracles stay arithmetic rather than host-dependent, while `fixedMetrics` in test/engine/reflow_test.go keeps that fake's proportional 0.5em because no reference face stands behind it. `atomicDemand` and `lineFrame.atomicTop` both have `atomicToMiddle` cases now and the bottom-edge stand-in is gone. The rule is the one this entry predicted - offset `base - xh/2 - extent/2`, demand `above = xh/2 + extent/2`, `below = extent/2 - xh/2` - and it is measured at sixteen parent sizes rather than fitted at one: a 4px chip on the 16px strut answers 18/7.8125, a 20px chip 20/0 with the block's text 0.1875 down the line, a 40px chip 40/0 text 10.1875, on a `line-height: 50px` strut 23.8125/15.8125/5.8125 for those three extents with the text at 16, 13.71875 at 24px, 19.625 at 32px, 40.25 for 4px and 22.25 for 40px at 64px. The half that GOOSIE-VALIGNTEXT-001 split off here closed with it: a run of text measures its own line-height box but keeps the PARENT's x-height, so a 16px/40px run on the 50px strut answers 16.8125 (the baseline stand-in measured 16, the bottom edge 21) and a 64px/74px run 0 on a line grown to 74 with the block's text at 27.1875. Oracle: 12 of the 32 rows in test/layout/middle_script_align_test.go, all red at HEAD 462fdb34; pixel: testdata/render/layout-features/10-middle-script-align.html 94.863% (iou 0.9899) against 74.599% FAIL pre-change. What this does NOT close is which x-height: the face gives OS/2 `sxHeight` (0.5234375em) and the reference positions on the ink box of 'x' (0.5229492em), a 1/64 px difference in position at 64px only - appended to GOOSIE-FONTMETRIC-001, which owns fidelity of the face.

owner: internal/layout (inline.go: vertical-align on a run of glyphs)
summary: Only atomic boxes consult their `vertical-align` value: a run of glyphs keeps the strut split whatever the class says, so `middle` and every length are no-ops on text, and `super`/`sub` are proportional guesses that move the box instead of growing the line.
evidence: Opened 2026-11-12 by the BR-272 slice: `demandOfRun` hands the parent's `strutMetrics` to `atomicDemand` for atomic runs and takes only `fontHeights` for text runs, so a glyph run's demand never reads `Style.VerticalAlign`. Measured on Chromium 2026-11-12 with `wordstail` in a 16px sans-serif block (line height, offset of the span's border box from the line top): `5px` -> 23, 0 (the run rises and the line grows on the far side of the baseline); `-5px` -> 23, 5; `middle` -> 18.8125, 0.8125; `super` -> 24.328125, 0; `sub` -> 22.1875, 4.1875. `cmd/dump-layout` on the same markup answers 18/0 for `5px`, `-5px` and `middle`, and 18/-8, 18/+6 for `super`/`sub` - those last two being the old `contentH*0.5` and `contentH*0.2` heuristics, which shift the box instead of stretching the line, so each row comes out 6.3px and 4.2px short and everything under a stack of them drifts up. The same heuristics measured on an atomic box in the same slice: `super` answers 2.8 where Chromium answers 3.67, and `sub` 13.6 against 14.19, for a 4px chip. `top`/`bottom`/`text-top`/`text-bottom` on a text run are NOT distinguishable on that markup - a run's own box coincides with the strut and Chromium answers 18/0 for all four - so a mixed-size line is needed before those four can be pinned; recorded as unmeasured rather than assumed fixed. What closing needs: give a text run the same two-sided currency as an atomic box (a length shifts both of its sides, an edge value stretches the line) and replace the super/sub fractions with measured reference metrics. ADDENDUM/CLOSED 2026-11-12 by BR-273 (e934dbbc) for every value that resolves from the metrics this interface already reports. A text run's alignment box is its own line height - `extent = lineH`, `above = asc + half`, `below = lineH - above`, `half = (lineH - (asc+desc))/2` unclamped - and `demandOfRun` sends that box through the same `atomicAlign`/`atomicDemand` path an inline-block uses, content top being box top + half. Measured against Chromium (Playwright 2026-11-12, 800x600, standards mode; 16px face 14/4/18, 64px 59/15/74) for a 16px run with `line-height:40px` on a 50px strut (30 above / 20 below): content top `baseline 16 / top 11 / bottom 21 / 5px 11 / -5px 21`, `text-top` 27 on a 56px line, `text-bottom` 11 on a 56px line with the block's own text at 22; for a 64px run with `line-height:74px`: `top` line 74 text 16, `bottom` 74/40, `text-top` 90 with the run at 16, `text-bottom` 90 with the run at 56, `5px` 84/50, `-15px` 74/30; and a `line-height:10px` run at 64px (half-leading -32) on the 18px strut answers line 18 with the ink at -32 for `top`, -24 for `bottom`, where the pre-fix engine built a 31px line. The four edge values this defect recorded as **unmeasured** because a same-size run cannot show them are now pinned on mixed-size rows: `test/layout/vertical_align_text_test.go` (3 tests, 69 assertions, tag `// qc:BR-273`), 32 of them red on the tree before the change while every row the old model already answered stayed green. Pixel evidence: `testdata/render/layout-features/09-text-run-align.html` 95.35% PASS (`worst_region_iou 0.99777`, `coverage_ratio 0.97031`, 0 blank bands) against 85.58% FAIL for the pre-fix binary on the same corpus (`iou 0.0`, `coverage 0.77459`, blank_regions 1/0, rows [(106,111)] shifted 1 - that band is ink on the wrong row, not ink lost); corpus 112/112 at average 96.45%, parity exit 0, `MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES` 111 -> 112. Split off instead of left implicit: `middle` on a run is now the same missing x-height as the atomic case (reference 16.8125 for a 16px/40px run on the 50px strut; the baseline, which is what this slice chose, is off by 0.8125 where the line's bottom edge would be off by 4.1875) -> GOOSIE-VALIGNMIDDLE-001, and `super`/`sub` keep their ratio guesses, measured further here -> GOOSIE-VALIGNSUB-001.

owner: internal/layout (inline.go: the super/sub offset on a run of glyphs), fed by a script metric no metric interface reports
summary: `vertical-align: super` and `sub` on a run of text are ratio guesses (`contentH*0.5` up, `contentH*0.3` down) applied after the line's extent has settled, so the box moves and the line does not grow: every such row comes out 6.33px (`super`) or 4.19px (`sub`) short and everything below a stack of them drifts up.
evidence: Split off GOOSIE-VALIGNTEXT-001 when BR-273 (e934dbbc) closed the classes that resolve from ascent, descent and line-height; these two need a number the interface does not carry. Measured on Chromium (Playwright 2026-11-12, 16px sans-serif, viewport 800x600, standards mode) for `words sup more` on the 18px strut: line box **24.328125**, the block's own text **6.328125** below the line top and the run at **0** - the offset is a constant **6.328125px** (0.3955em) that moves the *baseline*, so the line grows and carries the rest of the row with it rather than the run being lifted out of a fixed line. `sub` on the same row: line **22.1875**, text **0**, run **4.1875**, and 4.1875 is exactly half the x-height (8.375 from the OS/2 table; canvas `measureText('x').actualBoundingBoxAscent` answers 8.3672 because that is ink, not the metric), so `sub` closes with the x-height `middle` already needs (GOOSIE-VALIGNMIDDLE-001) while `super` needs the superscript offset. On a `line-height:50px` block the shift is the same 6.328125/4.1875 while the line answers **56.328125** with the text at **22.328125** (`super`) and **54.1875** with the text at **16** (`sub`) - which is what proves the offset belongs to the line's extent rather than to the strut. `cmd/dump-layout` on the same markup answers lines **18** and **50** with the run **8** above the text and **6** below it, so the placement error is 1.671875/1.8125px and the height error 6.328125/4.1875px per row. The same fractions on an atomic 4px chip answer 3/14 against the reference's 3.671875/14.1875, within rounding, which is why the atomic path is not the blocking part. What closing needs: superscript/subscript offsets - and the x-height - in the `Metrics` interface (internal/layout/arena.go), the host face's values in internal/raster/fonts.go, the fake `Metrics` the layout oracles already inject carrying them so an oracle stays arithmetic instead of host-dependent, and the offset charged to the two sides of the run's box in `runDemand` rather than subtracted from a placed `Y`. Blast radius is every superscript, footnote marker and chemical formula in the corpus: the vertical position of the whole row moves, so it must be scored by `make parity` and not only by unit oracles - `layout-features/09-text-run-align.html` and `typography/*` are the fixtures to watch. Nothing here is encoded from memory: the eight line/text/run numbers above are the reference answers for the markup in the probe (/tmp/strut/super.html, kept out of the tree because the corpus owns its own fixtures). ADDENDUM 2026-11-13, CLOSED by BR-275 (456f10d5). Both readings this entry carried are refuted by measurement. `sub` is not half the x-height - that arithmetic happens to match at 16px (4.1875) and nowhere else - and `super` needs no script metric either: the pair is `trunc_1/64(size/3) + 1` raised and `trunc_1/64(size/5) + 1` lowered, read from the PARENT's size, verified at fourteen sizes from 8 to 80px (12px 5/3.390625, 16px 6.328125/4.1875, 24px 9/5.796875, 32px 11.65625/7.390625, 64px 22.328125/13.796875). Because the quantity is a size rather than an edge, both values became lengths: `atomicAlign` sorts them into a new `atomicToScript` class, `resolveScript` writes the parent's number into `atomicBox.length` and reclassifies it as `atomicToLength`, so the existing demand/placement machinery charges the shift to BOTH sides of the box and the line grows - the proportional `line.h * 0.4` / `contentH * 0.5` / `contentH * 0.3` nudges that moved an already-placed box are deleted from BOTH placement sites in `inlineInto` - the shifted-subtree run path and the run-box path; the block-row path in `blockIntoInner` never had one, it only had to be handed the strut numbers. Measured after the change: the 18px strut with `super` on a text run answers line 24.328125 with the block's text 6.328125 below the line top and the run at 0 (pre-change 18 and the run 8px above the text); `sub` 22.1875/4.1875; a 4px chip 3.671875 (`super`) and 14.1875 on a line 18.1875 (`sub`); a 40px chip `super` 50.328125 with the text at 32.328125 and `sub` 40 with the text at 21.8125; at 64px a 4px chip 32.671875/68.796875; pure text at 12/16/24/32/64px lines 19/24.328125/37/48.65625/96.328125 (`super`) and 17.390625/22.1875/33.796875/44.390625/87.796875 (`sub`). The parent, not the box: a 24px run in a 64px block is lowered by 13.796875 - the 64px number - giving box 50.796875 on a line 78.796875, and a 64px run in a 16px block is raised by 6.328125. ``/`` are deliberately exempted from the shift in `resolveScript`, because the reference's `` computes `display: ruby-text` with `vertical-align: baseline` (measured via getComputedStyle 2026-11-13) and lays ruby out by its own algorithm; that residual is GOOSIE-RUBYALIGN-001. Oracle: the remaining 20 of the 32 rows, all red at HEAD; blast radius as predicted, the whole row moves, but the property's earlier fixtures did not regress: re-scored over the corpus they are identical (`layout-features/09-text-run-align.png` stays iou 0.9978 coverage 0.9703, every `typography/*` unchanged) and the two that changed moved toward the reference - `basic/02-inline-elements.png` 94.977 -> 96.475% (iou 0.1144 -> 0.7237, coverage 0.5176 -> 0.8254) and `edge-cases/04-empty-elements.png` 97.973 -> 98.110% (iou 0.8403 -> 0.9686).

owner: internal/layout (inline.go: ruby annotation placement, and the exemption in resolveScript) + internal/style/style.go (the UA rule that gives <rt> vertical-align: super)
summary: Ruby annotations are placed by a proportional raise rather than by a ruby algorithm, so the annotation overflows the block instead of making room for it: Chromium grows a 16px block to 27px to carry an 8px <rt> above the base text where Goosie keeps it at 18px with the annotation 2.2px outside, and puts <rtc> above the base where the reference puts it beside.
evidence:
Opened 2026-11-13 by the BR-275 slice, which had to decide whether the 's UA `vertical-align: super` (internal/style/style.go:688 gives { display: inline-block; font-size: 50%; line-height: 1; vertical-align: super }) should take the script shift that slice closes. It does not, and the check went both ways. Measured on Chromium (Playwright 2026-11-13, viewport 800x900, body margin 0, 16px sans-serif): the computed style of an is `display: ruby-text`, `vertical-align: baseline`, `font-size: 8px`, so the reference never resolves the declaration as a script shift, and its geometry reserves a band -
baseann
answers div height **27**, the base text's rect **9..27**, the rect **0..9** (9px tall for an 8px face, so 1px of leading); with in markup between base and rt the div answers **26**, base **8..26**, **-1..8**, and measures **y=8..26, x=34.703125, w=8** - on the base line to the right of the base text, not below it, and no below-band is reserved. Goosie on the same markup (in-process layout with the Chromium-shaped fake metrics test/layout/control_baseline_test.go installs) answers **18** for both divs, the box at **-2.2** with height 8 and its 18px line-box at **-16.2**, the and at **-18** with height 0 and the 's text 0..18: every annotation is overflow, none is reserved, and is above the base rather than beside it. The numbers are identical digit-for-digit between the pre-change binary (462fdb34) and the BR-275 one, which is what the exemption buys - the script answer on a 16px parent is 6.328125px and would drop the annotation into the base text it belongs above. Why P3: no fixture in testdata/render/ uses ruby and no interaction fixture does either, so nothing in the scored corpus depends on annotation placement; the observable consequence is a document whose ruby is clipped at its own top edge. What closing needs: a ruby placement rule of its own (measure the annotation band, grow the block by it, decide which side takes against the reference rather than by markup order), a fixture under testdata/render/typography/ or layout-features/ scored in the corpus, and only then a decision on whether the UA `vertical-align: super` on should stay at all - if ruby is laid out by ruby code the declaration is a hint, and keeping it while the script shift exists invites the two rules to fight. Not measured, and deliberately not encoded: Chromium's band with `ruby-position: under`/`over`, an annotation face other than 50%, multi-line ruby, and `ruby-merge`.

owner: internal/layout (strut in a BackCompat document), fed by internal/dom Document.QuirksMode
summary: Quirks mode is parsed and then never read, so a document without a doctype still gets the standards-mode strut: the reference drops the strut from a line whose content is all atomic, and every such row is 14px taller in Goosie.
evidence: Opened 2026-11-12 while the BR-272 oracle was being measured - it is why that oracle's markup carries ``. Measured 2026-11-12 on one document in both modes (body 16px sans-serif, viewport 800x600, `.row` divs holding a 40x4 inline-block chip): without the doctype Chromium reports `compatMode = BackCompat` and answers row heights 4, 4, 18 for the bare chip, the same chip with `vertical-align: top`, and `words` - so the strut is dropped exactly from the lines whose content is all atomic, while a line carrying text keeps its 18 - and with the doctype those three rows answer 18, 18, 18. `cmd/dump-layout` on the no-doctype file answers 18, 18, 18, i.e. the third row starts at y=36 in Goosie against Chromium's y=8: 14px per row, compounding down the page. Mechanism read from the code, not guessed: `dom.Document.QuirksMode` is set from the doctype (internal/dom/insertion_modes.go:658-687) and nothing in internal/css, internal/style or internal/layout consumes it. Scope to measure before implementing: the strut is the one quirk rule these numbers confirm; percentage heights, table borders and the `img` baseline are separate measured questions, and GOOSIE-DOCTYPE-001 covers only the doctype node's own position in the tree. What closing needs: the mode reaching the Arena, `ofStrut` suppressed for a BackCompat block's atomic-only lines, and a second run of the atomic-line oracle in quirks mode so both answers are pinned instead of one.

owner: internal/layout (block.go: replacedSize default widths) + internal/raster (no per-character measure, advances keyed on an integer size)
summary: A control's default WIDTH is a constant here while Chromium derives it from the font's per-character measure: the same text field is 153 wide at the 13.3333px UA font and 258 under an author 24px, and this engine answers 153 for both.
evidence: Opened 2026-11-13 by BR-276, which put the UA control font into the cascade and re-derived the intrinsic boxes, so widths became the visible half of the same defect instead of part of a sizing mystery. Measured on Chromium (Playwright 2026-11-13, viewport 800x600, standards mode, body 16px sans-serif, the same 29-row table test/layout/control_ua_box_test.go pins) against `cmd/tmpcontrolprobe` on the identical document: an empty text field is **153x21** at the UA font and **258x34** under `.big { font-size: 24px }` - here **153x21** and **153x34**, i.e. the height follows the font and the width does not; a textarea with `cols=20` is **182x36** where Goosie answers **161.9375x36**; a select sized by its option label is **30x19** at the UA font and **36x31** at 24px where Goosie answers **154x19** and **154x32** (the width is the engine's old 150px default plus 2px listbox chrome, which `replacedSize` still carries); the file control's **253x21** does match because it is a measured constant. The label-driven widths are short by a constant ratio: `button "Go"` **33.796875** vs 33.34375, `submit` **57.5** vs 56, `reset` **50.828125** vs 50, `input[button] "Go"` **33.796875** vs 33 - the three ratios are 0.9745, 0.9739, 0.9838, all ~2.5%, and ~2.5% is what 13.3333 rasterised as 13 costs; at an integer 24px the same path is exact (**48.015625x34** in both engines), so the shortfall is a fractional-size effect, not a broken text measure. That cause is read off the ratios, not out of the rasterizer, and is stated as such. Measured 2026-11-13 on https://www.gov.vn (viewport 1280, dpr 1) with a probe wired exactly like the browser (WithScripts/WithLinkedCSS/WithImages on net.DefaultClient). Immediately after NewSession - scripts already run - `#form1` reports style.display "none", opacity "1", document.body.scrollHeight 0. Pumping the same session for 800 ms in 10 ms slices ends with display "", opacity 0.4217827674798844 (other runs: 0.33063, 0.46077, 0.49214), jQuery.timers 1, body.scrollHeight 9514 and #form1 rect height 5028.283203125; a 4000 ms pump ends with opacity "1" and timers 0, i.e. the reveal is a jQuery fadeIn that needs paced event-loop turns. The shipped run instead writes nothing: `goosie -backend headless -width 1280 -height 1024 -dpr 1 -screenshot -url https://www.gov.vn/ -out gov.png` exits 0 in 6.45 s (fixed) and 7.04 s (HEAD 41024c5c) and the PNG is 6,109 bytes holding exactly 1 distinct colour, 0 non-white px (PIL getcolors). A frame at opacity 0.42 would hold many colours, so the captured frame is the display:none one: the settle decision (steadyFloorFrames 8 then two consecutive idle frames, ceiling frames*8, deadline 25 s - cmd/goosie/drive.go:118-135) is satisfied by frames during which the reveal's first timer has not run. Related and separate: GOOSIE-LIVE-003 records that a deadline give-up is indistinguishable from a settle. What closing needs: a readiness signal that counts pending JS work (queued timers, jQuery.timers) as not-idle, set from measurement of pages that reveal on a timer, not by lengthening the floor until the picture appears. BR-283 closed the half of this entry that named the mechanism, and the measurement says which half is left. The settle decision now consults the document's own load-phase timer queue: a timer armed while readyState != complete carries a beforeLoad mark (cleared at its first fire, so a booting interval counts only until then), Runtime.PendingLoadTimerDelay()/Session.PendingLoadTimerDelay() report the earliest such due (child browsing contexts included through a new eachIFrameChild), and cmd/goosie/drive.go holds a screenshot run while that due sits inside steadyRevealHorizon = 500ms, resets the idle count, and gives up after one horizon of its own wall clock. Both bounds come from measurement, not from taste: live timer dumps give gov.vn 81 timers armed before its load event with the non-white area not moving at all across 150/250/500/1250ms probes, vnexpress 938 timers with exactly one move 156,858,060 -> 159,597,862 between 200 and 300ms, tuoitre 327 timers moving at 200 and 300ms 351,555,917 -> 355,378,465; waiting for ALL pending timers was rejected because a 100ms heartbeat page and gov.vn's 24-hour boot timer would hold an entire sweep. Delay sweep on a controlled page (400x300 rgb(200,0,0) box behind display:none, 600x400 DPR 1, ink = non-white px by PIL; HEAD 0.219/0.234/0.194/0.196/0.185s, fixed 0.235/0.226/0.398/0.503/0.184s): HEAD ink 120,000 at 0ms and 100ms but 0 at 200/400/800ms (it settled 150-190ms after start); fixed ink 120,000 at 0/100/200/400ms - matching Chromium 131.0.6778.33 captured at load+1s (2 colours, 120,000 ink) - and still 0 at 800ms, where the cost measured exactly 0. Oracles: 18 tests tagged // qc:BR-283 (5 internal/js/pending_load_timer_test.go, 6 test/engine/pending_load_timer_test.go, 7 cmd/goosie/reveal_settle_test.go including three e2e that go through run([]string{"-screenshot", ...}) and decode the PNG). HEAD-red (worktree 7aa435c8, only the three e2e can compile there): ink = 0 px. Mutations M1-M8 on the fixed tree each killed its own oracle; M5 (horizon widened to 24h) killed only TestSteadyDoesNotWaitForLateStartupTimer, recorded as-is rather than paid off by loosening an oracle. No render fixture was added, and that is a measurement too: Chromium captured AT LOAD on the same page also reads 0 ink, so the page is timing-sensitive and would score a clock rather than an engine; instead both binaries were scored on the same corpus and the same Chromium references - fixed 119/119 (100.0%) average 96.57% exit 0, HEAD 119/119 (100.0%) average 96.57% exit 0, and 119/119 Goosie PNGs byte-identical (md5), which is what grep already predicted (0 fixtures in testdata/render use setTimeout/setInterval/requestAnimationFrame). WHAT THIS ENTRY STILL OWNS, measured: six runs of `goosie -backend headless -width 1280 -height 1024 -dpr 1 -screenshot -url https://www.gov.vn/` on the fixed binary read 1 distinct colour / 0 ink five times (6.66-8.33s) and 94 colours / 4,818 ink once (9.60s); HEAD read 1 colour / 0 ink at 7.29s. The page's own reveal is a jQuery fadeIn that the BR-282 probe placed at opacity 0.42 after an 800ms pump and opacity 1 with jQuery.timers 0 after a 4000ms pump - further out than the 500ms horizon and re-armed from inside the fade - so this slice does not recover it. The entry therefore stays open, narrowed to: reveals further out than the measured horizon, or armed after the load event. goosie-headless is deliberately untouched: that path is the operator-chosen -pump budget already recorded under BR-261, while -screenshot has no such knob.

summary: document.styleSheets lists only inline <style> elements: a document with three linked sheets and one inline block reports 1 where Chromium reports 4, and a live page reports 2 against 31 <link> elements.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSOMSURFACE-001. Measured 2026-11-13 on one fixture served over http - /tmp/t1/domgap/index.html, 469 bytes: 3 `<link rel=stylesheet>` (a.css, b.css, c.css, each answered 200), 1 `<style>`, 3 `<script>`, 2 `<a>`. Chromium: `document.styleSheets.length` 4, hrefs [a.css, b.css, c.css, null], `document.styleSheets[1].ownerNode.nodeName` "LINK". Goosie: length 1; the same href map answers "null" - the only entry is the inline sheet - and the ownerNode branch reports 'no ownerNode'. The cascade is unaffected: the same session applies each linked sheet's colour (BR-282's oracles read those colours), and the fixed engine issues exactly 3 stylesheet requests on the fixture where Chromium issues 3. On https://www.gov.vn the same gap reads Goosie 2 against Chromium 32 while both count 31 `<link>` elements. Registering rather than fixing because the honest scope is a CSSOM surface, not a fetch: closing needs styleSheets to expose one CSSStyleSheet per applied sheet with href, ownerNode and cssRules measured against Chromium, and the ordering rule (document position, imports after their parent) measured rather than assumed. ADDENDUM 2026-11-13, CLOSED by BR-284. Measured on a wider fixture served over http - /tmp/b284/index.html, 10 `<link rel=stylesheet>` (one `disabled`, one `media=print`, one duplicate href, one 404, one script-appended) + 5 `<style>` (one inside `<template>`, one `disabled`, one carrying an `@import`): Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (Node Playwright 1.63.0, /tmp/b284 probes) reads 12 entries and this engine read 4, every one of them owner STYLE. Now 12, in Chromium order LINK#L1..L7, STYLE#S1, STYLE#S2, LINK#L9, STYLE#S3, STYLE#S5. Per entry, both sides: `href` absolute for a link (equal to HTMLLinkElement.href) and null for a `<style>`; `media` the attribute verbatim plus a MediaList (`mediaText`, `length`, `item(0)`, `[0]`, `toString`); `title` "Alternate" or null; `type` "text/css"; `disabled` the sheet's own flag; `sheet === styleSheets[i]` true; `cssRules[0] === cssRules.item(0)` true; `String(sheet)` "[object CSSStyleSheet]". Two behaviours were measured rather than read off the spec and they shaped the fix: `<style disabled>` is both listed AND applied (HTMLStyleElement has no IDL `disabled`) while `<link disabled>` is neither - that is a real cascade miss, `p.dis` rgb(6, 6, 6) -> rgb(0, 0, 0) matching Chromium while `p.styledis` stays rgb(14, 14, 14) as Chromium's does; and a media-mismatched sheet is still fetched and still listed with its rules (`/print.css` 200, 1 rule at a screen viewport) even though the cascade ignores it - the old engine never requested it. The mechanism is one document-order walk (`styleSheetOwners`) that both the list and an element's `.sheet` go through, plus a callback channel `SetLinkedCSSProvider` -> `Session.StyleSheetText` -> BR-282's `cssText` memo, because archtest forbids internal/js from importing internal/engine. 14 oracles (9 test/js/style_sheets_surface_test.go, 5 test/engine/cssom_style_sheets_test.go) are all red on engine HEAD (worktree e9087fb4); the 12 mutations run on the fixed tree (M1-M11, M13) each kill at least one oracle, with one survival recorded as-is: dropping the URL dedupe outright kills no new oracle because BR-282's request-count tests already guard that path. The parts of the original scope this slice did NOT deliver are registered as separate entries rather than papered over: GOOSIE-CSSIMPORTRULE-001, GOOSIE-CSSOMMUTATION-001, GOOSIE-CSSTEXTSPACING-001, GOOSIE-CSSOMCOLLECTION-001, GOOSIE-STYLETEXTRULES-001; the script-added-links half narrows to GOOSIE-SCRIPTCSS-001, which stays open.

summary: Date.prototype.toGMTString is missing, and it is the single uncaught script error a real government page throws on every visit.
evidence: GOOSIE-DATEGMTSTRING-001. Measured 2026-11-13: Goosie `typeof Date.prototype.toGMTString` "undefined" and `new Date(0).toGMTString()` throws `Object has no member 'toGMTString'`; Chromium has the method as a function returning "Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT", byte-identical to its own toUTCString - which Goosie already answers correctly ("Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT"), so the formatting is in reach. Consequence on the live page: https://www.gov.vn recorded exactly one uncaught script error before this slice's changes, `TypeError: Object has no member 'toGMTString' at setCookie (https://f-emc.ngsp.gov.vn/embed/gov-tracking.min.js:2:32502) at setVisitorIdCookie` - a visitor-cookie helper dies on it. toGMTString is a legacy alias, so closing is one method delegating to the existing UTC formatting, measured on the epoch and one later date rather than assumed. CLOSED 2026-11-14 (BR-294): internal/js/date_legacy_alias.go installs Date.prototype.toGMTString delegating to the existing native toUTCString, so the GMT formatting is byte-identical by construction and the receiver check is preserved. Oracles test/js/date_gmt_string_test.go (3, qc:BR-294): typeof==function and own on the prototype, new Date(0).toGMTString()=="Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT" and a later epoch, toGMTString()===toUTCString() on an arbitrary timestamp, and toGMTString.call(42) throws TypeError. Two mutations on the fixed tree, byte-identical restores: removing the setup call kills the first two oracles with typeof==undefined; swallowing the receiver error (panic->return) kills only the non-Date-receiver oracle. This closes the named visitor-cookie script error on www.gov.vn; it does not touch the other GOOSIE-LIVE-001 rows.

evidence: GOOSIE-CSSIMPORTRULE-001. Measured 2026-11-13 on the /tmp/b284 fixture over http, both sides after load. Goosie fixed: `importType` 1 (the object handed back is the p.b style rule, its `cssText` "p.b { color: rgb(0,10,0); }"), `importHref` absent, `importStyleSheet` null, b.css 1 rule first "p.b", S1 1 against 2. The cross-access identity this entry deliberately left unprobed is now measured, and it came with a law nobody had guessed: a CSSRuleList is a snapshot - a fresh read after a text edit reports the edited rules while the handle already held keeps its old ones and `after === before` is false - whereas the StyleSheetList and the MediaList stay live through the one object a page holds. Registered rather than papered over: GOOSIE-CSSRULEWRAPPER-001 (the sheet and rule wrappers), GOOSIE-CTORMESSAGE-001 (`new` wording), GOOSIE-STYLETEXTRULES-001 (the cascade half, corrected there), GOOSIE-CSSOMMUTATION-001 (appendMedium/deleteMedium, insertRule/deleteRule). GOOSIE-DOCCOLLECTIONS-001 was suggested as a companion pass and is untouched: document.scripts and document.links are still absent. Cross-build re-measurement 2026-11-13: the same 14 /tmp/b287 probes run on the pinned render oracle (Playwright 1.49.1, Chromium 131.0.6778.33), one fresh page load each, agreed on 12 of 14. The two that split are `liveAfterAttr` - 131 keeps the old text on a held MediaList (`screen, print,2,screen,print,screen, print,0+1`) and hands a different object on re-read, 153 answers the new text through the same object - and `protoOfProtoName`, null on 131 against undefined on 153, which no oracle reads. This engine follows the 153 reading, which is the live view the interface defines. The 39-probe CSSOM list over the same fixture family (/tmp/b286, one fresh browser context per probe) was re-run on both builds the same day: 38 of 39 identical. The one that split is `mediaOneQueryComma`, which appends a <link> whose href the page already fetched - the warm-href reading recorded on GOOSIE-LINKSHEET-001 - and it is not a MediaList question: the MediaList text both builds report from it is the same whenever the sheet is there at all. An earlier version of this cross-check ran every probe on one shared page and reported 37 of 39; the two extra differences were DOM and cache state leaked from earlier probes, not browser behaviour, and are withdrawn.

owner: internal/js + internal/css (a <style> whose textContent changes after load)
summary: A <style> whose textContent is edited never changes this engine's computed styles while Chromium follows it synchronously: a removed rule leaves rgb(10, 0, 0) here where Chromium reads rgb(0, 0, 0), and a rule the edit added computes rgb(0, 0, 0) here against rgb(9, 9, 9).
evidence: GOOSIE-STYLETEXTRULES-001. Measured 2026-11-13 on file:///tmp/b286/index2.html, a `<style>` holding two rules at parse time whose textContent gains a third synchronously after load. Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (the Node Playwright 1.63.0 oracle that ran it): the handle taken at load reports 2 rules at load, in the same task, after 2 requestAnimationFrame ticks, after 200 ms and after appending a matching element - yet `getComputedStyle` of that element reads rgb(9, 9, 9), so the new rule is certainly applied, and a fresh `document.styleSheets[0].cssRules` read at the same moment reports 3, which is BR-285's snapshot law. Re-run twice each on the pinned render oracle 131.0.6778.33: every reading identical, 2 at load, 2 through the whole held-handle sequence, 3 on the fresh read, rgb(9, 9, 9) and rgb(10, 0, 0). Goosie (BR-284's tree): the CSSOM goes 1 -> 2 because `sheetRuleObjects` keys its cache on the sheet's text and rebuilds when the text differs. The rendering half agrees with Chromium on both binaries, which is why this is P3. What is explicitly NOT measured is when Chromium reparses: "2 rules at every probe" is a timing observation on a synchronous edit, not a reading of Blink's dirty-flag machinery, and it does not prove the list is never rebuilt. Closing needs that timing pinned down first (probe at several distances from the edit, and probe the case where the edit drops a rule rather than adding one) so a fix can copy the observed behaviour instead of guessing which side of the CSSOM/update boundary the reparse belongs on. ADDENDUM 2026-11-13, BR-285: the CSSOM half of this entry is not a divergence and has been corrected by measurement. Across four edit shapes on a link-free http document (/tmp/b287/index12.html, cr_col12.txt against go_col12.txt) Chromium's next `cssRules` read reports the edited rules (replace -> `2,p.z`, append -> `3,p.a`, shrink -> `1,p.z`) and the handle captured before the edit keeps its old rules with `after === before` false - which is exactly what BR-285's snapshot list answers, so the earlier "Chromium does not reparse into cssRules, still 2 rules at every probe" was an artefact of probing only a handle taken before the edit (and, in the other fixture, of a linked sheet that also matches the tested element). What is left, and is now the whole entry, is the cascade: on that same document Chromium drops a removed rule synchronously (`#P` reads rgb(0, 0, 0)) and applies a rule the edit added to a freshly appended matching element (rgb(9, 9, 9)), while this engine keeps the colours it resolved at load (rgb(10, 0, 0) and rgb(0, 0, 0)). Closing needs the invalidation path for a sheet whose text changed, measured first for how far it reaches - an element already in the tree against one appended after the edit - and the timing question this entry opened with is no longer the blocker.

summary: RESIDUAL after BR-309: a CSSStyleRule now exposes a live, WRITABLE `style` (CSSStyleDeclaration) whose setProperty/removeProperty, named camelCase setter, cssText replacement and index/name deletion mutate the rule's own declarations and stay self-consistent on the handle. GOOSIE-CSSRULEWRAPPER-001. NARROWED AGAIN 2026-11-15 by BR-301 (3b0efc73), after BR-299 (2319e31a) closed the own-property leak and rule branding. summary: A <link> a script appends is listed with a usable sheet in the same task here, where Chromium 153.0.8010.12 answers `link.sheet === null` until its fetch lands and only Chromium 131.0.6778.33 hands a sheet back in the task when the href is already in the page's cache: this engine reads `[object CSSStyleSheet]` with the list already grown (5 where both builds still say 4), and the sheet holds its rules only if the URL was fetched by the markup, never a fresh request.
evidence: GOOSIE-LINKSHEET-001. owner: docs hygiene; the fix is a verifier in the gate suite, no engine decision needed
summary: `file.go:NNN` citations in docs drift silently and nothing in CI notices. The 2026-11-14 comment strip forced a full re-derivation (1,148 citation numbers in 66 docs now differ from the pre-strip HEAD, counted off the diff) and that work measured the shape of the problem: of 1,561 citation tokens in the 119 tracked docs, 298 are quoted tool output that must never be re-pointed, 352 name a bare filename the re-deriver cannot resolve (99 of them an ambiguous basename), 26 are `, :NNN` continuations riding on a preceding reference, and 21 use a short-form path (`paint/builder.go:13`, `headless/window.go:145`) that resolves to no file as written - 14 of those are only missing the `internal/` prefix and 1 (`internal/debug/render_debug.go:219,231`) names a file the tree deleted. `go test ./...` is green with every one of those tokens broken, so a doc can be confidently, invisibly wrong. Measured the same way, only 33 of 132 citations that name a Go symbol and a line number actually land on that symbol, and 93 of 900 resolvable citations land on a line holding nothing but a brace.
evidence: Measured on the 2026-11-14 tree while re-deriving every citation after removing 32,893 comment-only lines and 683 trailing comments (both counted off the diff) from first-party Go. The re-derivation itself: 1,177 numbers resolved in 66 docs - 1,148 of them land on a different file or line than HEAD does, which is the count a reader can reproduce from the diff; the 1,177 and the tier mix below are the migration tool's own verdict counts - tier mix 924 moved-exact 924 moved-exact / 213 comment-anchor-moved-exact / 26 exact / 10 decl / 2 comment-anchor-decl / 2 trimmed-note, 292 transcripts preserved verbatim, 1 flag (the dead `render_debug.go` reference above), and `go test -count=1 ./...` rc 0 with 48 packages ok on the final tree - i.e. the suite is no obstacle to a stale doc. Three proofs that a resolvable line is not the same as the right line. (1) `docs/analysis/parity-gap-2026-10.md:23` cites `testdata/parity.py:51-70, 534-535` for 'explicit 800x600, DPR 1'; at f56ff8aa (2026-10-26 - the same day that doc was written) lines 51-70 hold the corpus-floor ratchet comment and the viewport defaults are at 217/239/265/285, so the citation was ~166 lines off at authoring time and no tool could have caught it by content. (2) GOOSIE-LIVE-002 named `internal/engine/limits.go:226 (float64 overflow)` where the refusal actually sat at 242 - 16 lines off pre-strip; after the strip the mechanical re-derivation answered 186 (it followed the `switch t.Type {` text, still 9 lines short of the branch the prose describes), so I hand-pointed that phrase to 195/199/204 and said so in the entry. (3) Two claims whose only evidence had been a code comment were withdrawn rather than re-pointed: an '8 MiB fetch cap' (no such constant exists anywhere in the tree; the note it quoted read `MaxResponseBytes = 16 MiB`) and a multi-line-flex 'explicitly single-line' row (falsified - `layoutFlexRow` internal/layout/block.go:492, line count 631-650, `distributeFlex` 791, `layoutFlexColumn` 1022, 13 tests in test/layout/flex_multiline_test.go). Why it matters: this repository's honesty rule is that a number names a measurement, and a line citation is a claim that a reader can go and read; silently-unresolvable citations turn the registry into unverifiable prose, and the comment strip removed the fallback (a reader could once grep the quoted sentence and find the line). Proposed closing shape, not yet built: a gate test that extracts every citation token from docs/, classifies colon-adjacent tokens as transcripts to skip, resolves bare names only when the basename is unique, and fails on a missing file, a number past EOF, or a blank line; plus a prose rule that a citation anchors on a declaration or a test assertion rather than a bare interior line of a long function, because declarations survive edits and interior lines do not. Measured further the same day, on the phrase shape where a check is possible at all: of 132 citations that name a Go symbol and a line number within the same phrase, 33 put that symbol within 3 lines of the number and 99 do not. Hand-verified misses, all of them older than the strip: `Session.Reflow` cited `internal/engine/engine.go:874` and declared at 1393; `PumpJS` cited 1574, declared 2555; `matchesChecked` cited `internal/css/selector.go:1323`, declared 1385; `inheritFromParent` cited `internal/style/style.go:2133`, declared 2149; `Session.NewSession` cited `engine.go:140`, which is the struct field `touches map[string]*dom.Touch`, while `engine.NewSession` is declared at 422; `Session.PaintChecked` cited `engine.go:506`, which is `s.workCounts.styleResolves.Add(1)`, while the method is in `internal/engine/paint.go:13`. A second shape measure: 93 of the 900 resolvable live citations land on a line holding only `}`, `{` or `)` - 82 on a bare brace - so the number names a position and nothing a reader can check. Two classes turned out to be format, not drift: 13 of the 21 short-form citations resolve as written once the `internal/` prefix is added (`paint/builder.go:13` -> `internal/paint/builder.go:13`), and 7 non-functional comments survived the strip only on lines carrying multi-byte text, because Go reports a comment column as a byte offset while the cutter sliced by characters - residue like `{"שלום hello", 0, 1}, // f` and `f.Glyph(16, '中', slot) //`. Those 7 are now cut and an AST re-scan of all 1,033 first-party Go files reports zero non-functional comments: 1,019 tokens left, 1,003 `// qc:BR-NNN`, 12 `//go:build`, 4 cgo preamble blocks. Fixed in this task, and the reason the entry asks for a verifier rather than another sweep: AGENTS.md (5 citations) and PROJECT.md (12), so all 19 citations in those two files now land on the declaration the prose names - `engine.NewSession` 422, `Session.PaintChecked` internal/engine/paint.go:13, caps internal/engine/limits.go:23-50, decode caps internal/image/decode.go:16-20, the import table internal/archtest/rules.go:20-52, cascade order internal/style/style.go:1517-1553, `Reflow` internal/engine/engine.go:1393. owner: cmd/goosie/document_loader.go (display-list extent -> layer bounds) and internal/raster/scheduler.go clampScroll
summary: The scroll ceiling is the extent of the painted display list, not the layout height, so the trailing unpainted blocks of a page are unreachable: the same document scrolls to y=920 in Chromium and to y=320 in Goosie.
evidence: GOOSIE-SCROLLCEILING-001. Found while pinning BR-287's one-screen scroll (2026-11-14), measured on two byte-level twins at 600x400 DPR 1, one PageDown screen = 360 px. Fixture: 20px margin, a 300px red block, a 300px spacer, a 60px blue marker at y 640..700, then a 600px tail block - 1320px of layout. Variant PLAIN gives the tail no background; variant PAINTED gives it only `background:rgb(250,250,250)`. Goosie, `./goosie -screenshot-seq ... -seq-scroll-screens 5`: PLAIN reports scroll_y 320 after 2 presses (the third press moved nothing), PAINTED reports 920 after 4 presses. Chromium 131.0.6778.33 (Playwright, same two files, `window.scrollTo(0,99999)`): BOTH reach scrollY 920, and it reads `documentElement.scrollHeight` 1320 with `clientHeight` 400 on both - an empty block still contributes its border-box to the scrollable overflow region. The 600px shortfall is exactly the unpainted tail. Mechanism, read from the source and consistent with both numbers: cmd/goosie/document_loader.go:574-588 takes `extent := dl.Extent()` from the built display list and passes it to `frame.NewLayer`, so the layer bounds - and `paint.SceneSpec.DocHeight`, and the gate report's `doc_height` - are the painted extent; internal/raster/scheduler.go resolveLocked/clampScroll then clamp every scroll to those bounds, so the ceiling is shared by wheel, PageDown, the -gate driver and the new -seq-scroll-screens press. Consequence for a user: the bottom of any page whose last blocks paint nothing (spacer divs, a reserved gap, a lazy container that has not revealed) cannot be reached by scrolling, and a scrolled capture of it is silently short. Not measured here: whether the engine's own layout root reports 1320 for PLAIN - there is no scrollHeight or document-height accessor to ask it (that gap is registered separately), so the claim rests on the 320-vs-920 pair on identical layout and on Chromium's measured 1320. A fixing slice should size the layer from the layout document height (the root box's margin-box bottom, i.e. what scrollHeight must return) rather than from the display-list extent, keep the painted extent as a separate budget input if the tile cache needs it, and re-measure both variants; BR-287's fixture deliberately paints its tail so the oracle pins the scroll law instead of this defect, and its catalog row says so. ADDENDUM 2026-11-14, live numbers from the BR-288 measurement of https://about.google/products/ (1280x1024 dpr 1, Chromium 131.0.6778.33, binary sha 5938f539188bfefc...). Oracle scrollable range for that page is `scrollHeight - innerHeight` = 6,832. Goosie asked for N screens reports, per run, scroll_y = N*921 up to 20 screens (921, 1,842, 2,763, 3,684, 5,526, 7,368, 11,052, 18,420) and, asked for 30, stops after 26 presses at scroll_y 22,917 - so on this page the ceiling this entry describes is 3.35x the oracle's rather than short of it, because the law is working on Goosie's own painted extent and that extent reaches at least 23,941px (22,917 + a 1,024 viewport). Ink per capture, parity.ink_mask: 1,219,268 at 921; 1,268,578 at 1,842; 873,421 at 2,763; 878,909 at 3,684; 1,018,559 at 5,526; 11,197 at 7,368; 0 at 11,052; 0 at 18,420; 377 at 22,917 - every one of them with idle=true, tiles_needed=0, painting_bytes=0. Read carefully, because it cuts both ways for this entry: the clamp is not the bug here (the document really is that tall to this engine), so a fixing slice that sizes the layer from the layout document height must re-measure this page instead of assuming the range will shrink - what is wrong is upstream, in how tall and how empty that layout is, and that is registered as GOOSIE-SCROLLRANGE-001. Also worth keeping from this run: the press loop stops counting when an extra press moves nothing, so `scroll_presses` < requested `scroll_screens` in frames.json is how a clamped ceiling becomes visible at all. ADDENDUM 2 2026-11-14 (BR-289): after the minified at-rule prelude fix the same live page's ceiling measured through `-seq-scroll-screens` falls from 22,917 (26 presses) to 19,349 (23 presses), and the last capture still holds almost no ink (377 -> 995 px) - the ceiling keeps tracking Goosie's own painted extent exactly as this entry predicts, so it shrinks only as fast as the layout bug upstream does. One caveat this slice measured and wants recorded before anyone quotes a ratio: Chromium's own reported scrollable range for that URL is NOT stable across navigations - 6,832px in three runs and 9,576px in a fourth (/tmp/b289x-top-pre.json) - so 'Goosie scrolls 2.8x too far' is only defensible as '2.0-2.8x', against a page whose oracle height itself moves.

summary: An at-rule whose prelude opens with `(` - `@supports(display:grid)`, `@media(min-width:600px)` - was read as one long at-keyword, matched no dispatch case, and was skipped as an unknown at-rule, so every declaration inside the block never reached the cascade. Registered and closed by the same slice (BR-289) because the defect was found while measuring its own symptom.
evidence: GOOSIE-ATPRELUDE-001. Found by the first scrolled live pass (GOOSIE-SCROLLRANGE-001, BR-288), which described about.google/products' card list as `glue-grid__col--span-4` items laid out in full-width bands and explicitly refused to name a cause. The cause is here and it is one character class: `atRuleName` scanned the keyword until `{`, `;` or whitespace, so `@supports(display:grid)` produced the name `supports(display:grid)`, the dispatch switch had no such case, and the parser took its unknown-at-rule path - which drops the body. Google's shipped bundle writes these preludes with no space before the `(`, so the whole grid system of the page was invisible to the cascade; `internal/layout/grid.go` was never involved. Red evidence measured on the old parser: the 1280px fixture reports `card 0 = x 0 y 0 w 1136, want x 0 y 0 w 346.6667` and `ul.H = 400, want 248` - the exact full-width band shape the live capture showed, produced because grid.go:147-152 collapses a container with no tracks to one auto column - and on the CSS side `rulesText("@media(min-width:600px){.wide{}}@media(max-width:600px){.narrow{}}") = ""`, i.e. both blocks vanish rather than the wrong one matching. Fix, three sites: `atRuleName` also stops at `(`; a new `atRuleCondition` returns the prelude from its first `(`/`{`/`;`/whitespace, replacing the old `IndexByte(' ')`+`TrimPrefix` pair that returned a condition-less string for the minified form; and the keyword-skip loops in parseContainerRule and parseScopeRule stop at `(` so `@container sidebar(max-width:600px)` keeps its query text. One candidate change was **reverted rather than shipped**: the same `(` stop added to parseLayerRule's keyword loop survived the whole mutation matrix (m5a SURVIVED) and `@layer(...)` is not a valid CSS form, so no oracle could have pinned it; after the revert exactly two loops carry the `(` stop, and the mutation script confirms it by reporting SITE NOT FOUND for a third site. Oracles: 10 tests tagged `// qc:BR-289` (8 test/css/at_rule_prelude_test.go, 2 test/layout/grid_minified_at_rule_test.go); 7 are red on the old parser, and the 3 that are green on HEAD by design - no-prelude `@media{}`/`@font-face`, `@unknown(abc)` still dropped, `print and (min-width: ...)` kept intact - are guards against over-fixing, not proof of the defect. Mutation matrix on the fixed tree: m1 (keyword does not stop at `(`) killed 5 css + 2 layout; m2 (condition keeps the at-keyword) 6 css + 2 layout; m3 (condition cut at the first `(` instead of the first condition character) 4 css; m4 (`@supports` accepting any feature) 3 css; m5a container-loop and m5b scope-loop variants each killed by the query-text oracle. Parity proof, fixture `testdata/render/grid/03-minified-at-rule-cards.html` (corpus row 120, `MIN_SCORED_FIXTURES` raised in the same commit): 24.581% FAIL on the pre-fix binary (sha 7116e630..., coverage 1.3005, worst_region_iou 0.7989) -> 99.572% PASS (coverage 1.0, iou 1.0, 0 blank bands); corpus 119/120 avg 95.971 -> 120/120 avg 96.596 with exactly one row moved, re-scored identically after the layer revert (final binary sha 0af9c9f8...). Live A/B on the page that hid the defect (scripts/live-frame-stability.py, 1280x1024 dpr 1, Chromium 131.0.6778.33): the scrolled pass at y=921 moves from 11.56% to 14.51% exact-within-tolerance, worst_iou 0.463 -> 0.504, coverage 1.842 -> 1.925, Goosie ink 1,219,268 -> 1,177,486 against Chromium's 244,520 (4.99x -> 4.82x), and the depth ladder drops at every level asked (2,763: 873,421 -> 511,405; 4,605: 424,640 -> 227,495; 7,368: 11,197 -> 3,017) with the scroll ceiling falling 22,917 -> 19,349. That is the direction this entry predicts but not its closure: GOOSIE-SCROLLRANGE-001 stays open for the remaining 4.82x, and the top pass regressed, which is registered as GOOSIE-TOPPARITY-001 rather than explained here.

summary: When a -screenshot run has its response routed to the downloader, it must write a determinate reason to stderr (naming the URL and the header that triggered the route) and exit with a code a caller can distinguish from a render failure.
evidence: Split out of GOOSIE-CTYPE-001 on 2026-11-14; BR-296 (be4e16c2) fixed only the ShouldDownload classification. The phrasing carried here since then — "exits 1 without stating on stderr that the answer was a download" — was PARTIALLY FALSIFIED by measuring the real binary before this slice: a download-routed -screenshot already printed `goosie: downloaded to <path>` on stderr, so the run was not silent. The two honest residuals that were real: (1) the stderr line named only the saved path, not the URL or which header (Content-Disposition vs Content-Type) caused the route; (2) EXIT=1 was indistinguishable from a rendering failure, so a caller could not separate "this URL is a download" from "this page failed to paint" (the GOOSIE-LIVE-003 failure class). Closed by BR-303: downloadDone carries url/contentType/contentDisposition; run() wraps it as screenshotDownloadError only for the screenshot path with the message `goosie: no screenshot for <url>: the response was routed to the downloader (<Content-Disposition or Content-Type>), saved to <path>; nothing to paint`; exitCodeFor returns 3 for the download signal, 2 for usage, 1 otherwise. Measured on the built binary after the fix: download route -> EXIT=3 + full message + no PNG; text/html -> EXIT=0 + PNG; connection refused -> EXIT=1 (distinct, no over-trigger). Four oracles in cmd/goosie/screenshot_download_route_test.go, red under three mutations (drop URL/trigger, hardcode exit 1, drop the wrapper). Scope honesty: this changes only the report and exit code, not the classification (BR-296) and not any attempt to render a downloaded document.
